query:
Portainer: fast coordinator fetches unfiltered docker system df every 60s but uses only the volume section

### The problem

The main `PortainerCoordinator` calls `docker_system_df()` **unfiltered** on every 60 s refresh, but consumes only the volume section of the result. On hosts where `docker system df` is slow, this makes dockerd walk the entire image layer chain once a minute to produce data that is then discarded — and where the call exceeds the coordinator's 10 s `request_timeout`, the refresh is abandoned while the daemon keeps working, so the host pays the full CPU cost and receives nothing at all.

I think this is the remaining half of #164965 / #165702. #165855 (thanks for that) correctly moved the *DF sensors* onto `PortainerDockerDiskSpaceCoordinator` at 30 minutes with a 120 s timeout and a deferred first refresh. But the same call is still in the fast path, at [`coordinator.py#L264`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/80632caf2eadb5a154f1c53990e02264ca79768d/homeassistant/components/portainer/coordinator.py#L264), inside the `asyncio.gather`:

```python
self.portainer.docker_system_df(endpoint.id, verbose=True),
```

The only thing read from the result is at [`coordinator.py#L376-L380`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/80632caf2eadb5a154f1c53990e02264ca79768d/homeassistant/components/portainer/coordinator.py#L376-L380):

```python
volume_usage_map = {
    item["Name"]: item
    for item in (docker_system_df.volume_disk_usage.items or [])
}
```

i.e. `Items[].UsageData.Size` and `Items[].UsageData.RefCount`. The image, container and build-cache sections are computed by the daemon and thrown away — and the container section is essentially the whole cost.

**Why abandoning the request does not help.** The fast coordinator's client is built with `request_timeout=10`. When the df call takes ~58 s, pyportainer gives up at 10 s, `except PortainerTimeoutError: continue` skips the endpoint, and no data is produced for that cycle. dockerd, however, does not stop. Measured directly — a request with a 10 s client timeout, then watching the daemon:

```
baseline            dockerd  0.0% / 0.1% of one core
curl exited rc=28 after 11s
t=+10s              dockerd 88.8% of one core
t=+20s              dockerd 81.1%
t=+30s              dockerd 80.7%
t=+40s              dockerd 70.4%
t=+50s              dockerd 87.0%
t=+60s              dockerd 14.5%
t=+70s              dockerd  0.2%
```

~55 s of work after the client had already walked away, repeating every 60 s. I believe this explains the otherwise puzzling report in #164965 that "Portainer data stopped importing into HA until I deleted the entry, but the CPU continued regardless" — those two symptoms are the same cause, not two problems.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.9.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Not a regression from a specific version — present since the `system/df` call was added to the coordinator.

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Portainer

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/portainer

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Timeout error while accessing GET http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/endpoints/1/docker/system/df:
```

Intermittent, against the 10 s `request_timeout` on the fast coordinator's client. Note that a slow-but-successful refresh logs nothing at `warning`, so on most affected hosts the only visible symptom is dockerd CPU.

### Additional information

**Environment.** Home Assistant Container 2026.9.1, pyportainer 1.0.45, Portainer CE 2.39.7, Docker 29.8.0, overlay2 on ext4. Amlogic S905X3, 4 cores, 1.8 GiB RAM, root on an SD card. Portainer runs on the same host (`http://127.0.0.1:9000/`), so none of this is network latency.

**`docker system df` split by resource type:**

| `GET /system/df?type=` | time |
|---|---|
| `image` | 0.8 s |
| `volume` | 0.2 s |
| `build-cache` | 0.1 s |
| **`container`** | **50.7 s** |

The container section is the entire cost, and it is `SizeRootFs`. Per container:

| container | time |
|---|---|
| mosquitto | 0.9 s |
| portainer | 0.2 s |
| **homeassistant** | **55.5 s** |

This is **not** about object count — this host has 5 images, 3 containers and 2 volumes. It is 8.1 GB / 339k inodes of overlay2 on slow storage with too little RAM to keep the dentry cache warm, so a repeat call is just as slow as the first. For reference `du -s /var/lib/docker/overlay2` takes 41.7 s warm and `docker ps -s` takes 57 s, so Docker's own CLI is equally affected; the integration is only what triggers it every minute. The Home Assistant image is itself the container that makes the call expensive, which is a large part of why this bites HA users specifically.

**Through the Portainer API,** which is what the integration actually calls:

| request | time | keys returned |
|---|---|---|
| `?verbose=true` (current) | **57.8 s** | `ImageUsage`, `ContainerUsage`, `VolumeUsage`, `BuildCacheUsage` |
| `?verbose=true&type=volume` | **0.1 s** | `VolumeUsage` |

Identical `Items[].UsageData.{Size,RefCount}` payload — verified against a live instance.

Every other call in the same refresh is cheap: containers 0.81 s, container stats 1.75 s, inspect 0.29 s, version 0.37 s, info 0.28 s, volumes 0.06 s, stacks 0.16 s.

**Effect.** At the default 60 s interval dockerd sat at **107 % of one core** continuously, load 2.4 — about a quarter of this box, permanently. Setting `pref_disable_polling` on the entry drops dockerd to **0.3 %** and load to 0.2. Confirmed by counterfactual: stopping only the Portainer container took dockerd from 107 % to 0.1 %.

Also worth knowing: `_perform_action()` ends in `async_request_refresh()`, and `pref_disable_polling` suppresses only *scheduled* refreshes. So even with polling disabled, every switch toggle triggers one full refresh — meaning each container start/stop costs an ~60 s state-update lag on an affected host.

### Suggested fix

`pyportainer` already exposes the filter, so this is two lines:

```diff
 from pyportainer.models.docker import (
     DockerContainer,
     DockerContainerStats,
+    DockerDFType,
     DockerSystemDF,
     DockerVolume,
     DockerVolumeUsageData,
     LocalImageInformation,
     PortainerImageUpdateStatus,
 )
@@
-                    self.portainer.docker_system_df(endpoint.id, verbose=True),
+                    self.portainer.docker_system_df(
+                        endpoint.id, data_type=DockerDFType.VOLUME, verbose=True
+                    ),
```

**Verified.** I am running exactly this as a patched copy of the integration on the box described above, with polling re-enabled at the default 60 s. Coordinator debug timings across consecutive cycles:

```
Finished fetching portainer data in 0.239 seconds (success: True)
Finished fetching portainer data in 5.833 seconds (success: True)
Finished fetching portainer data in 65.473 seconds (success: True)
Finished fetching portainer data in 0.931 seconds (success: True)
Finished fetching portainer data in 0.214 seconds (success: True)
Finished fetching portainer data in 1.067 seconds (success: True)
Finished fetching portainer data in 0.187 seconds (success: True)
Finished fetching portainer data in 0.190 seconds (success: True)
Finished fetching portainer data in 0.156 seconds (success: True)
```

Steady state 0.16–1.07 s, dockerd 0.1 % of one core, load 0.14, no coordinator timeouts.

The 65.5 s outlier is honest and worth noting: that is the fast refresh colliding with `PortainerDockerDiskSpaceCoordinator`'s own (correctly) unfiltered call, which still walks the tree once every 30 minutes. So the contention is not eliminated, only reduced from every 60 s to every 30 min. If that remains a problem for very slow hosts, the DF coordinator's interval or its `type` breakdown might be worth revisiting separately — but its sensors do expose `container_disk_usage` and `image_disk_usage`, so it genuinely needs the expensive sections and 30 minutes seems a reasonable place to pay for them.

Correctness checks on the trimmed response:

- Every field on `DockerSystemDF` has a default, so the omitted sections deserialise to `None` rather than raising. Confirmed by feeding a volume-only payload through `DockerSystemDF.from_dict()` and rebuilding `volume_usage_map` from it: keys present, `Size` and `RefCount` carried through intact.
- Volume size/refcount sensors are unchanged in behaviour on my instance.
- `tests/components/portainer/conftest.py` sets `client.docker_system_df.return_value` on a mock that ignores call arguments, so this should be snapshot- and test-neutral.

Happy to open a PR for this if it would help — just say the word.

query:
Fix swallowed exceptions in color_extractor action handlers

The `color_extractor` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `services.py`:**
- `async_handle_service` (services.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

Fix swallowed exceptions in huawei_lte action handlers

The `huawei_lte` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `notify.py`:**
- `send_message` (notify.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

query:
MCP config flow initializes ClientSession twice, causing valid Streamable HTTP servers to fail -- including the solution

### The problem

## MCP config flow fails with a valid Streamable HTTP server due to double `initialize()`

### The problem

Home Assistant 2026.8.0 fails to add a valid Streamable HTTP MCP server.

The MCP server can be reached from the Home Assistant host, successfully completes the MCP `initialize` handshake, and exposes its tools correctly.

The same endpoint also works correctly with the same Python MCP SDK version used by Home Assistant (`mcp==1.26.0`).

However, adding the endpoint through:

Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → Model Context Protocol

results in:

> Connection failed

or, depending on the transport/server used:

> Unexpected error

I traced this to what appears to be a double initialization of the same `ClientSession`.

### Home Assistant version

Home Assistant Core: **2026.8.0**

Installation type: **Home Assistant OS**
Running as a VM on Proxmox.

### MCP server

The server exposes a standard Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint.

Example endpoint:

`http://<server>:12008/metamcp/home-assistant-websearch/mcp`

The particular server implementation is not important for reproducing the client behavior, but in my setup MetaMCP is used as the MCP endpoint.

It exposes four tools from an upstream SearXNG MCP server.

### Evidence that the MCP server works

A manual MCP initialize request succeeds:

    POST /metamcp/home-assistant-websearch/mcp

Response:

    HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    content-type: text/event-stream
    mcp-session-id: <session-id>

    event: message
    data: {"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26","capabilities":{"prompts":{},"resources":{},"tools":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":"metamcp-unified-...","version":"1.0.0"}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}

The `notifications/initialized` request succeeds:

    HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted

A subsequent `tools/list` request using the same session succeeds:

    HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    content-type: text/event-stream

and returns all four MCP tools.

The Streamable HTTP GET stream also opens successfully and remains connected.

### Reproduction using Home Assistant's MCP SDK version

I reproduced the connection outside Home Assistant using:

    python:3.13-slim
    mcp==1.26.0

Test code:

    import asyncio
    from mcp import ClientSession
    from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamable_http_client

    URL = "http://<server>:12008/metamcp/home-assistant-websearch/mcp"

    async def main():
        async with streamable_http_client(URL) as (read, write, _):
            async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
                result = await session.initialize()
                print("INITIALIZE OK:", result.serverInfo)

                tools = await session.list_tools()
                print("TOOLS:")
                for tool in tools.tools:
                    print("-", tool.name)

    asyncio.run(main())

Result:

    INITIALIZE OK: name='metamcp-unified-...' version='1.0.0'

    TOOLS:
    - SearXNG__searxng_web_search
    - SearXNG__searxng_search_suggestions
    - SearXNG__web_url_read
    - SearXNG__searxng_instance_info

Therefore the endpoint works with the MCP SDK used by Home Assistant.

### Suspected cause

In Home Assistant 2026.8.0, `mcp_client()` in:

`homeassistant/components/mcp/coordinator.py`

initializes the `ClientSession` before yielding it:

    async with (
        streamable_http_client(
            url=url,
            http_client=create_async_httpx_client(hass, headers=headers),
        ) as (read_stream, write_stream, _),
        ClientSession(read_stream, write_stream) as session,
    ):
        await session.initialize()
        yield session

The SSE fallback does the same:

    async with (
        sse_client(url=url, headers=headers) as streams,
        ClientSession(*streams) as session,
    ):
        await session.initialize()
        yield session

However, `validate_input()` in:

`homeassistant/components/mcp/config_flow.py`

initializes the same yielded session again:

    async with mcp_client(hass, url, token_manager=token_manager) as session:
        response = await session.initialize()

This means that during the config flow the sequence is effectively:

    ClientSession created
        ↓
    session.initialize()       # coordinator.mcp_client()
        ↓
    yield session
        ↓
    session.initialize()       # config_flow.validate_input()

The second `initialize()` appears to cause the connection/config flow failure with otherwise valid MCP servers.

### Local workaround / confirmation

I copied the 2026.8.0 MCP integration into:

`/config/custom_components/mcp`

and applied the following minimal behavioral change.

In `mcp_client()`, I removed both calls to:

    await session.initialize()

so the context manager only creates and yields the session:

    async with (
        streamable_http_client(
            url=url,
            http_client=create_async_httpx_client(hass, headers=headers),
        ) as (read_stream, write_stream, _),
        ClientSession(read_stream, write_stream) as session,
    ):
        yield session

and likewise for the SSE fallback.

Because other callers previously relied on `mcp_client()` initializing the session, I explicitly initialize it once at each call site.

In `ModelContextProtocolTool.async_call()`:

    async with mcp_client(
        hass, self.server_url, self.token_manager
    ) as session:
        await session.initialize()
        result = await session.call_tool(
            tool_input.tool_name, tool_input.tool_args
        )

In `ModelContextProtocolCoordinator._async_update_data()`:

    async with mcp_client(
        self.hass,
        self.config_entry.data[CONF_URL],
        self.token_manager,
    ) as session:
        await session.initialize()
        result = await session.list_tools()

`config_flow.validate_input()` already calls:

    response = await session.initialize()

so no additional initialization is required there.

### Result after patch

After restarting Home Assistant with this patched integration, the exact same MCP URL that previously returned:

> Connection failed

was immediately accepted.

Home Assistant displayed:

> Configuration for metamcp-unified-... created.

The MCP server subsequently appeared as a Tool Provider in the Local OpenAI LLM conversation agent.

After enabling the MCP Tool Provider, the conversation agent successfully used the exposed SearXNG tools to retrieve current web information.

For example, asking the agent for Home Assistant news from the current day returned current Home Assistant 2026.8 release information and current sources.

Therefore the complete path works after removing the double initialization:

    Home Assistant Conversation Agent
        ↓
    Home Assistant MCP integration
        ↓
    Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
        ↓
    MCP tools
        ↓
    Web search

No changes to the MCP server, Docker networking, HTTP transport, or MCP SDK were required between the failing and working tests.

### Expected behavior

A valid Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint that successfully completes `initialize()` and advertises the `tools` capability should be accepted by the MCP config flow.

A `ClientSession` should only be initialized once.

### Actual behavior

`mcp_client()` initializes the session and `config_flow.validate_input()` initializes the same session again.

The config flow rejects an otherwise working MCP endpoint.

Removing the duplicate initialization resolves the issue.

### Additional notes

The issue was reproduced with both a direct Streamable HTTP MCP server and while investigating an SSE compatibility path.

Extensive testing confirmed:

- network connectivity from Home Assistant to the MCP server
- successful HTTP connection
- successful MCP `initialize`
- valid `Mcp-Session-Id`
- successful Streamable HTTP event stream
- successful `notifications/initialized`
- successful `tools/list`
- successful operation using `mcp==1.26.0` outside Home Assistant
- successful Home Assistant configuration after applying the initialization patch

This strongly suggests that the failure is caused by the Home Assistant client lifecycle rather than the MCP server or transport.

query:
Silently failed forwarded platform setup wedges config entries into non-recoverable FAILED_UNLOAD on next unload

### The problem

When a forwarded platform's setup fails, the failure is silently discarded: `_async_forward_entry_setups_locked` gathers the per-platform setup tasks and ignores their results, and for forwarded domains `ConfigEntry.async_setup` explicitly does not store a failed result as state ("Only store setup result as state if it was not forwarded"). The owning config entry therefore ends up `LOADED` while one of its platforms was never registered in that domain's `EntityComponent` (`self._platforms`).

Everything appears to work — until the entry is next unloaded (user reload, reauth, options flow, or an integration-triggered reload). `EntityComponent.async_unload_entry` then raises `ValueError("Config entry was never loaded!")` for the phantom platform, `config_entries` converts that into a failed unload, and the entry lands in **`FAILED_UNLOAD` — a non-recoverable state**. Every subsequent reload attempt raises `OperationNotAllowed`; the only way out is restarting Home Assistant.

The net effect: a transient, invisible platform setup failure (e.g. a flaky cloud API during one reload) converts a later, perfectly normal unload into a restart-only outage. There is nothing to unload for the phantom platform, so failing the whole unload — and wedging the entry — serves no purpose.

This is not integration-specific. Reports of the same chain across the years:

local_todo fails to save Todo items containing non-ASCII characters

### The problem

local_todo fails to save Todo items containing non-ASCII characters.

The error occurs when store.py writes the generated ICS content using Path.write_text() without explicitly specifying UTF-8 encoding.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.9.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2026.8.x
 
### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

local_todo

### Link to integration documentation on our website

[_No response_](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/local_todo/)

### Diagnostics information

Logger: homeassistant.helpers.script.websocket_api_script

The error occurs when calling todo.add_item:

```txt
UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode characters in position 263-264: ordinal not in range(128)
```

Relevant part of the traceback:

```txt
File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/local_todo/store.py", line 36, in _store
    self._path.write_text(ics_content)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.14/pathlib/__init__.py", line 810, in write_text
    return f.write(data)
UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode characters in position 263-264: ordinal not in range(128)
```

### Reproduction

1. Create a Local Todo list.
2. Call todo.add_item.
3. Add an item containing only ASCII characters, for example Test.
  • Works successfully.
4. Add an item containing Chinese characters, for example 测试主卧清扫.
  • Fails with the UnicodeEncodeError above.

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml

```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

**Environment**

* Core: 2026.9.0
* Installation: Home Assistant Supervised
* Architecture: aarch64
* Machine: qemuarm-64
* Python: 3.14
* Integration: local_todo
* Service: todo.add_item


 **Workaround / verification**

I verified that explicitly specifying UTF-8 encoding fixes the issue.

Changing:

```python
self._path.write_text(ics_content)
```

to:

```python
self._path.write_text(ics_content, encoding="utf-8")
```

and restarting Home Assistant Core allows Todo items containing Chinese characters to be saved successfully.

This suggests that local_todo should explicitly use UTF-8 when writing the ICS file instead of relying on the default encoding.

### Additional information

I also noticed a separate issue after upgrading from the previous Core version: previously completed Todo items disappeared.

I am reporting this separately because I am not sure whether it is related to the encoding issue.

Tesla Fleet blocking HA Bootstrap when vehicle is asleep

### The problem


**The problem**
 
`tesla_fleet` blocks Home Assistant bootstrap while the vehicle is asleep, and when the stage-2 setup budget (300 s) expires the config entry is cancelled and never retries.
 
`async_setup_entry` calls `async_config_entry_first_refresh()`, whose first refresh goes to `api.vehicle_data()`. That call has no timeout of its own and does not return until the car answers. A sleeping Model 3 routinely takes several minutes to answer (it is not woken by the integration — by design, and correctly). The whole of bootstrap waits on it.
 
Measured on 3 Sep 2026 (times local, Australia/Perth):
 
- 09:31:52 — core startup otherwise complete
- 09:32:34 onward — `Waiting for integrations to complete setup: tesla_fleet, petkit` repeated once a minute; no other integration named
- 09:36:36 — `Setup of config entry ... for tesla_fleet integration cancelled` (and `petkit` 28 ms later, as collateral of the same budget expiry)
- 09:36:36 → 11:22:50 — all `tesla_fleet` entities `unavailable`; the entry sat in `setup_error`, which is not retried; it came back only when reloaded by hand
Traceback at cancellation ends in `async_config_entry_first_refresh` → `_async_update_data` → `api.vehicle_data()` → aiohttp response wait.
 
**What I expected**
 
Either (a) the first refresh should be bounded — e.g. wrap `vehicle_data()` in `asyncio.timeout(...)` and raise `ConfigEntryNotReady` so the entry lands in `setup_retry` and recovers on its own, or (b) the integration should not block setup on `vehicle_data()` at all when `vehicle()` reports the car offline/asleep, and instead set up with restored/unknown state and refresh on the next poll (the integration already knows how to do this once running — see the online check in the coordinator).
 
Either would turn a slow cloud response into a slow first poll rather than a failed setup that needs a human.
 
**What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?**
 
core-2026.8.3
 
**What type of installation are you running?**
 
Home Assistant OS (18.2), generic-x86-64
 
**Integration causing the issue**
 
Tesla Fleet
 
**Anything in the logs that might be useful?**
 
```
[09:32:34] Waiting for integrations to complete setup: tesla_fleet, petkit
... (repeats once a minute)
[09:36:36] Setup of config entry <redacted> for tesla_fleet integration cancelled
[09:36:36] Setup of config entry <redacted> for petkit integration cancelled
```
 
(Full traceback attached.)
 
**Additional information**
 
- A separate `Timeout fetching Tesla Fleet Vehicle data` on 2 Sep 21:48 cost 10 minutes of unavailable entities, which suggests the running-state coordinator does have a timeout path — the first refresh is the exception.
- Workaround in place locally: an automation that reloads the config entry when its entities read `unavailable` while an unrelated LAN device on the same link is healthy. It recovers inside ten minutes but is a net under the symptom.
- The 300 s stage-2 budget is not user-configurable, so a slow Tesla API response turns every restart into a lottery over which integrations survive it.

OpenHome: Linn players become temporarily unavailable without any logged exception

### The problem

I have two Linn OpenHome players:

- Linn Majik DSM
- Linn Sneaky DS

Both are connected via wired Ethernet with static IP addresses.

Occasionally the `media_player` entity becomes `unavailable` for about 4–5 seconds and then automatically returns to its previous state. Both have the same behaviour.

The audio playback never stops. Only Home Assistant temporarily loses control of the player.

Example:
playing -> unavailable
~5 seconds later
unavailable -> playing

The problem has existed for several years over many Home Assistant releases and several Linn firmware versions.

### What I have already verified

- Wired Ethernet
- Static IP addresses
- No WiFi involved
- No IGMP Snooping on the MikroTik bridge
- Linux Bridge in Proxmox without multicast filtering
- Both Linn devices respond immediately to HTTP requests
- SSDP advertisements are received correctly

- Source

query:
todo.item_added trigger stops firing after the list's config entry is reloaded

**The problem.** An automation with a `todo.item_added` trigger fires until the to-do entity's
config entry is reloaded. After the reload the entity is re-created and keeps updating — its
state (open-item count) changes when an item is added — but the trigger never fires again.
Turning the automation off and on restores it until the next reload.

**Reproduction, local only, two minutes** (verified 2026-09-03 on core-2026.7.4 Container):

1. Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → **Local To-do**, name it `Bug repro`.
   Entity `todo.bug_repro` appears.
2. Automation: trigger `todo.item_added` on `todo.bug_repro`; action
   `persistent_notification.create`, message `fired`.
3. Add an item to the list → notification. (`last_triggered` updates.)
4. Reload the Local To-do config entry (three-dot menu → Reload). Entity returns, state intact.
5. Add an item → state increments, **no notification, `last_triggered` unchanged**.
6. Turn the automation off and on; add an item → notification.
7. Reload again; add an item → dead again.

Same result on the Alexa Devices to-do platform (two reloads there too). Reloads of the
`shopping_list` integration cannot be used for this because it does not support reload
(`require_restart: true`).

**Where it comes from, as far as I can read it.** `homeassistant/components/todo/trigger.py`
subscribes with `entity.async_subscribe_updates(...)` on the entity *object* fetched when the
listener starts, and only re-runs `_start_listening` from
`TargetEntityChangeTracker._handle_entities_update`, which reacts to `entity_registry_updated`
events. A config-entry reload removes and re-creates the entity object but leaves the registry
entry as it is, and `EntityRegistry.async_get_or_create` emits no event when nothing changed
(`if not new_values: return old`). So the subscription stays attached to the discarded object.
This also explains why a reload that does change a registry field appears to "work".

**Suggestion.** Re-subscribe when the tracked entity object is added (entity component
`async_add_entities` / the entity's `async_added_to_hass`), or track the entity's state leaving
`unavailable`, rather than relying on registry events alone.

**Version:** core-2026.7.4, Home Assistant Container. Happy to test a fix.

I'll send a PR that re-subscribes when the entity comes back after reload, plus a regression test along the lines of your Local To-do repro.

query:
Fix swallowed exceptions in openhome action handlers

The `openhome` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `media_player.py`:**
- `async_media_next_track` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_pause` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_play` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_previous_track` (media_player.py)
- `async_media_stop` (media_player.py)
- `async_mute_volume` (media_player.py)
- `async_play_media` (media_player.py)
- `async_select_source` (media_player.py)
- `async_set_volume_level` (media_player.py)
- `async_turn_off` (media_player.py)
- `async_turn_on` (media_player.py)
- `async_volume_down` (media_player.py)
- `async_volume_up` (media_player.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

query:
Remove user-configurable polling interval from `upcloud`

The `upcloud` integration exposes `CONF_SCAN_INTERVAL` as a user-configurable field in its config flow. Polling intervals should be set by the integration author, not exposed to users.

Remove the polling interval field from the config flow and set a fixed interval in the coordinator or integration setup, per the [appropriate-polling quality scale rule](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/integration-quality-scale/rules/appropriate-polling).

Part of home-assistant/epics#45, which contains more information, including migration instructions.

+    coordinator: TibberDataAPICoordinator,
+    home_ids: set[str],
+) -> None:
+    """Migrate Data API registry entries to Tibber device IDs."""
+    entity_registry = er.async_get(hass)
+    entity_entries = er.async_entries_for_config_entry(entity_registry, entry.entry_id)

+
+    migrations: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
+    device_migrations: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
+    device_id_by_identifier = {home_id: home_id for home_id in home_ids}
+    for device in sorted(
+        coordinator.data.values(),
+        key=lambda device: (device.name != legacy_device_name, device.id),
+    ):
+        if (
+            legacy_device
+            and not device.external_id
+            and device.name == legacy_device_name
+        ):
+            device_id_by_identifier.setdefault("", device.id)
+        device_id_by_identifier[device.id] = device.id
+        if device.external_id:
+            device_id_by_identifier[device.external_id] = device.id
+        for sensor in device.sensors:
+            new_unique_id = f"{device.id}_{sensor.id}"
+            migration = (new_unique_id, device.id)
+            migrations[new_unique_id] = migration
+            if device.external_id:
+                migrations[f"{device.external_id}_{sensor.id}"] = migration
+            else:
+                # An empty external ID produced a legacy leading-underscore unique ID.
+                migrations.setdefault(f"_{sensor.id}", migration)
+
+    for entity_entry in entity_entries:

+            continue
+        new_unique_id, device_id = registry_migration
+        if entity_entry.device_id:
+            # Empty external IDs may have grouped multiple Tibber devices.
+            device_migrations.setdefault(entity_entry.device_id, set()).add(device_id)
+        if entity_entry.unique_id != new_unique_id:
+            entity_registry.async_update_entity(
+                entity_entry.entity_id, new_unique_id=new_unique_id
+            )
+
+    for registry_device in dr.async_entries_for_config_entry(
+        device_registry, entry.entry_id
+    ):

+            tibber_device_id = min(
+                (
+                    coordinator.data[device_id].name != registry_device.name,
+                    device_id,
+                )
+                for device_id in tibber_device_ids
+            )[1]
+        else:
+            expected_device_ids = {
+                device_id_by_identifier[identifier]
+                for domain, identifier in registry_device.identifiers
+                if domain == DOMAIN and identifier in device_id_by_identifier
+            }
+            if len(expected_device_ids) != 1:
+                device_registry.async_remove_device(registry_device.id)
+                continue
+            tibber_device_id = expected_device_ids.pop()
+
+        identifiers = {(DOMAIN, tibber_device_id)}

query:
Anthropic conversation agent: tools.N.custom.input_schema (JSON Schema draft 2020-12) 400 error persists on 2026.9.0, unrelated to custom integrations

### The problem

The Anthropic (Claude) conversation agent fails with a 400 error on every
single request when "Control Home Assistant" is enabled — including queries
completely unrelated to timers (e.g. "what was yesterday's solar peak").

Error from home-assistant.log:

2026-09-04 09:23:51.644 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.anthropic]
Error while talking to Anthropic: Error code: 400 - {'type': 'error', 'error':
{'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'message': 'tools.41.custom.input_schema:
JSON schema is invalid. It must match JSON Schema draft 2020-12
(https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12).'}, 'request_id': 'req_...'}

This looks related to the same root cause as #160565 / #160462 (HassStartTimer /
HassDecreaseTimer generating anyOf at the top level of input_schema). However,
those issues were reportedly fixed by stripping oneOf/anyOf/allOf in the
Anthropic entity code (homeassistant/components/anthropic/entity.py), and the
fix was later ported to the OpenRouter integration in #172153 explicitly citing
Anthropic's existing fix as the reference implementation. The error persisting
on 2026.9.0 suggests either a regression in that filtering logic, or a new tool
schema (not previously covered) that also violates the top-level
oneOf/anyOf/allOf constraint.

### Troubleshooting already performed

- Disabled a HACS custom integration (ha-mcp / ha_mcp_tools) entirely — error
  persisted unchanged, including the same tools index (41).
- Disabled specific custom-integration tools individually (raw YAML read/write
  tools) — error persisted unchanged.
- Tool index (41) remained stable across all of the above configuration
  changes, which suggests the offending tool is a **built-in** HA tool exposed
  via the Assist API, not a custom-integration tool — since a custom
  integration's tools being added/removed would normally shift indices of
  anything after them, but a built-in tool earlier in a fixed enumeration order
  would not move.
- Attempted to capture the full request payload via httpx debug logging, but
  httpx's default logger only logs method/URL/status, not the request body, so
  the exact tool name behind index 41 could not be confirmed this way.



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.9.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Unknown — the Anthropic conversation agent was working correctly before this was noticed; exact regression point not identified.

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Anthropic

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/anthropic/

### Diagnostics information

Model: claude-opus-5
Caching strategy: Full
"Control Home Assistant" (Assist API): enabled
prefer_local_intents: true (per Assist pipeline trace) — error occurs even
when the local sentence-based intent matcher does not claim the request first

### Additional information

Happy to provide the full JSON tools array from a debug capture if someone can
point me to how to get httpx to log the request body, or if there's a way to
dump the LLM API's tool schema list directly from Home Assistant (e.g. via
Developer Tools or a diagnostic service) without needing model-level debug
logging.

  File: homeassistant/components/homekit/type_covers.py:326-341 — OpeningDevice.async_update_state                                          
                                                                                                                                            
  Why the states appear inverted                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                            
  The iOS Home app doesn't derive the "Opening"/"Closing" label from the PositionState characteristic — it compares CurrentPosition vs      
  TargetPosition:
  - current < target → renders "Opening"                                                                                                    
  - current > target → renders "Closing"                                                                                                    
                                        
  Commit ac56b3306a8 (Aug 2022, PR #77101) changed the updater so that during motion it updates current_position but deliberately leaves    
  target_position alone. That was correct for HomeKit-initiated moves (target was already set to the final goal), but it breaks             
  externally-triggered moves:
                                                                                                                                            
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬───────────────────┬────────────────┬──────────────┬───────────┐                        
  │              Scenario               │ HA state │ Current (updated) │ Target (stale) │ iOS displays │ Expected  │

  Proposed fix

  In OpeningDevice.async_update_state, when the cover is moving, snap target_position to the movement endpoint only when it is inconsistent 
  with the reported direction. This preserves the existing fix for HomeKit-initiated partial moves (e.g. target=50), while correcting the

  @callback

          self.char_current_position.set_value(current_position)

tesla_fleet: a transient DNS failure leaves the config entry in SETUP_ERROR permanently

### The problem

A DNS resolution failure during setup leaves the `tesla_fleet` config entry in `ConfigEntryState.SETUP_ERROR`. That state is terminal, so Home Assistant does not retry it and the integration remains unloaded until it is reloaded manually. In our case the entry failed on 2026-07-26 and was only noticed 32 days later, when a dashboard built on the vehicle data was observed to be flat.

The condition is difficult to recognise from the UI. The entry is marked as failed, but no reauth flow is started and `supports_reconfigure` is `false`, so no remediation is offered. The symptoms also resemble an authentication problem: the stored token's `expires_at` becomes stale and the log records `Error resolving OAuth token: 400`. Both are consequences of the entry never loading rather than causes, and re-authorisation is not required — a reload is sufficient.

**Why it happens**

`tesla_fleet_api`'s `_request` logs and re-raises the original exception without wrapping it (`tesla_fleet_api/tesla/fleet.py`):

```python
except (Exception, TeslaFleetError) as e:
    LOGGER.debug("command=%s transport=%s result=error error=%s: %s", ...)
    raise
```

`aiohttp.ClientConnectorDNSError` therefore reaches the integration unwrapped. Its MRO is `ClientConnectorDNSError → ClientConnectorError → ClientOSError → ClientConnectionError → ClientError → OSError`, so it is not a `TeslaFleetError`.

`_async_get_products` converts only the library's own exception types:

```python
except (TeslaFleetError, OAuth2TokenRequestError) as e:
    raise ConfigEntryNotReady from e
```

so the aiohttp exception escapes `async_setup_entry`. In `config_entries.py`, only `ConfigEntryNotReady` results in `SETUP_RETRY` with backoff (`:803`); any other exception results in `SETUP_ERROR` (`:856`), for which no retry is scheduled.

One further detail explains why the outage persisted rather than resolving when the network recovered: the reload-on-connectivity-restored path applies only to entries in `LOADED` or `SETUP_RETRY` (`config_entries.py:3049`), so entries in `SETUP_ERROR` are not covered by it.

The coordinator path is unaffected. `_async_refresh` catches broad `Exception` (`update_coordinator.py:390`) and `async_config_entry_first_refresh` converts that into `ConfigEntryNotReady`, so the gap is limited to `_async_get_products`.

**Reproduction**

1. Make `fleet-api.prd.na.vn.cloud.tesla.com` unresolvable, for example by blocking DNS or pointing the resolver at an unresponsive server.
2. Restart Home Assistant, or reload the `tesla_fleet` entry.
3. Restore DNS.
4. The entry remains in `setup_error`. No retry is scheduled, no reauth flow is started and no repair issue is raised; a manual reload is required to recover.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.4.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_Not a regression; the behaviour is also present on `dev` (`ed14d7c2`)._

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

tesla_fleet

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tesla_fleet

### Diagnostics information

_Not attached: the entry could not be loaded, so diagnostics were unavailable while the fault was present._

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../aiohttp/resolver.py", line 117, in resolve
    resp = await self._resolver.getaddrinfo(
aiodns.error.DNSError: (12, 'Timeout while contacting DNS servers')

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:
  File ".../aiohttp/resolver.py", line 126, in resolve
    raise OSError(None, msg) from exc
OSError: [Errno None] Timeout while contacting DNS servers

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 769, in __async_setup_with_context
    result = await component.async_setup_entry(hass, self)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tesla_fleet/__init__.py", line 155, in async_setup_entry
    products = await _async_get_products(tesla)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/tesla_fleet/__init__.py", line 68, in _async_get_products

  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/tesla_fleet_api/tesla/fleet.py", line 183, in products
    return await self._request(
```

### Additional information

**Suggested fix**

Treat transport-level failures as transient in `_async_get_products`, consistent with the existing handling of `TeslaFleetError`:

```python
except (
    TeslaFleetError,
    OAuth2TokenRequestError,
    ClientError,
    TimeoutError,
) as e:
    raise ConfigEntryNotReady from e
```

`TimeoutError` is listed separately because `asyncio.TimeoutError` is not a subclass of `aiohttp.ClientError`.

`tests/components/tesla_fleet/test_init.py` already parametrises this path through `SETUP_ERRORS` / `test_init_error`, which mocks `products()` and asserts the resulting entry state, so the regression coverage is two additional rows in that table. They fail against current `dev` with `assert <ConfigEntryState.SETUP_ERROR> is <ConfigEntryState.SETUP_RETRY>` and pass with the change applied.

A PR is ready and will be linked here shortly.

**Alternative, or complementary**

Wrapping transport errors in `TeslaFleetError` within `_request` in `tesla_fleet_api` would address this for all consumers of the library rather than Home Assistant alone. That may be preferable in the longer term, though it depends on a separate release cycle, and it seems reasonable for the integration not to rely on the library never surfacing a transport exception. Happy to raise that separately if it would be useful.

**Versions**

`tesla-fleet-api` 1.4.5 as pinned by 2026.4.1; `dev` currently pins 1.10.0, and the `_request` behaviour above is present in both.

Bond: config flow overwrites a working CONF_HOST with the other interface of a dual-homed bridge

### The problem

The Bond Bridge Pro is dual-homed. Olibra's documentation states the bridge
announces itself on *every* network it is connected to, so a bridge on both Wi-Fi and Ethernet
answers to one `<bondid>.local` hostname at two IP addresses, and both serve the local HTTP API.
Ethernet is preferred for cloud traffic while Wi-Fi is kept associated as a live backup.

`ZeroconfServiceInfo.host` is documented as "the most recently updated address that is not link
local or unspecified", with `ip_addresses` holding all of them. On a dual-homed bridge that makes
`host` whichever interface refreshed its mDNS record last — effectively a coin flip that can
re-flip on any refresh.

`bond/config_flow.py::async_step_any_discovery` then writes that value unconditionally:

```python
updates = {CONF_HOST: host}
return self.async_update_reload_and_abort(entry, data={**entry.data, **updates}, ...)
```

So a working entry gets moved onto the idle Wi-Fi interface. The Wi-Fi radio power-saves, and the
result is intermittent `TimeoutError` on `/v2/devices/{id}/state`, covers flipping to
`unavailable`, and the entry occasionally going `setup_retry`. Users experience this as "Bond keeps
changing IP".

## What I observed

Bond Bridge Pro (Olibra `zermatt-pro`, firmware v4.34.1) driving shades:

| Interface | MAC | IP | Bond app status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wi-Fi | `F4:4E:38:xx:xx:C4` | `192.168.7.243` | "Connected" |
| Ethernet | `F4:4E:38:xx:xx:C7` | `192.168.7.250` | "Connected to cloud" |

HA had stored `host: 192.168.7.243` — the Wi-Fi address — captured by zeroconf at setup.
Roughly 28 timeout occurrences in a single day. Disabling Wi-Fi on the bridge fixed it completely;
HA then moved itself to `.250` via zeroconf and has been stable since.

Note the DHCP matcher in `bond/manifest.json` (`"macaddress": "F44E38*"`) matches **both**
interfaces, so the DHCP discovery path can move the host too.

## Suggested fix

Don't rewrite a host that is still valid. In `async_step_any_discovery`, if
`entry.data[CONF_HOST]` is present in `discovery_info.ip_addresses`, leave it alone:

```python
if entry.data.get(CONF_HOST) in [str(ip) for ip in discovery_info.ip_addresses]:
    updates = {}
else:
    updates = {CONF_HOST: host}
```

That preserves the genuine self-heal (bridge actually moved) while removing the spurious
interface flip.

## Prior reports with the same signature

- #110178 — Bond Bridge Pro + 27 Somfy shades, `TimeoutError` on the state endpoint, 1–5 covers
  unavailable at a time. Closed stale; nobody connected it to dual-homing. 
- #140963 — same family of local-API action failures.

Both are closed **and locked**, which is why this is a new issue rather than a comment.

## References

- Ethernet — Bond Home Technical Documentation (Chris Merck, CTO Olibra):
  https://tech.bndh.io/technical/ethernet/
- Forum post linking it: https://forum.bondhome.io/t/bond-bridge-pro-a-note-on-ethernet/5889
- `helpers/service_info/zeroconf.py` — `host` = most-recently-updated address

Withings: webhook subscription races HA's own HTTP server on startup and never retries

### The problem

`WithingsWebhookManager` subscribes the webhook shortly after setup. Withings validates a `notify/subscribe` call by sending an **HTTP HEAD to the callback URL** — i.e. the request has to travel out to the internet and back into this Home Assistant instance.

On a slower host (RPi 4) that round trip lands **before HA's own HTTP server is accepting connections**, so the probe fails, Withings answers with "The callback URL is either absent or incorrect", and `_async_subscribe_webhook` logs an error and `return`s:

```python
except WithingsInvalidParamsError as err:
    LOGGER.error("Webhook URL rejected by Withings: %s", err)
    return
```

Unlike `WithingsTooManyRequestsError` and the generic `WithingsError` branches right below it, this branch schedules **no retry**. The webhook therefore stays unsubscribed for the entire uptime and the integration silently falls back to polling.

### Evidence that it is a startup race, not a misconfiguration

Home Assistant restarted at 07:17:44. The error is logged at 07:18:36:

```
2026-09-10 07:18:36.966 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.withings] Webhook URL rejected by Withings: The callback URL is either absent or incorrect
```

At that exact second, the reverse proxy in front of the instance logs Withings' probe arriving and being unable to reach the origin:

```
2026-09-10T05:18:36Z ERR Request failed error="Unable to reach the origin service. The service may be down or it may not be responding to traffic from cloudflared: dial tcp 10.0.0.2:8123: connect: connection refused" dest=https://example.tld/api/webhook/<redacted> ip=198.41.192.107 type=http
```

`connection refused` on HA's own port — HA had not started listening yet.

Once startup finished, the *identical* URL worked immediately. Calling `notify/subscribe` by hand against the same callback URL returned `{"status": 0}`, and `homeassistant.reload_config_entry` on the Withings entry subscribed all six categories:

```
status 0 | subscriptions: 6   (appli 1, 4, 16, 44, 50, 51)
```

Before the reload, `notify/list` returned `{"status": 0, "body": {"profiles": []}}` — zero subscriptions. This reproduces on every restart.

### Suggested fix

Treat `WithingsInvalidParamsError` as retryable, at least for the first few attempts, the same way the sibling `except` branches already do — or delay the initial subscription until `EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STARTED` plus a grace period, since the call fundamentally requires HA's HTTP server to be reachable from the internet.

Likely the same underlying cause as the closed #117420 ("Withings - Stops working after reboot").

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.9.0 / 2026.9.1

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS (raspberrypi4-64)

### Integration causing the issue

withings

UniFi Protect doorbell message select resets custom messages after 60 seconds

## The problem

The UniFi Protect integration no longer keeps custom doorbell LCD messages displayed indefinitely.

Previously, using the UniFi Protect `Doorbell text` select entity displayed the message indefinitely. After upgrading Home Assistant, the message now disappears after approximately 60 seconds.

## Environment

- Home Assistant: 2026.9.1
- UniFi Protect: 7.2.105
- Device: UniFi G4 Doorbell
- Integration: `unifiprotect`

## Reproduction

1. Open the UniFi Protect doorbell device in Home Assistant.
2. Set a custom message using the "Doorbell text" dropdown.
3. Observe that the message is removed after approximately 60 seconds.


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2026.5.4

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

unifiprotect

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/unifiprotect/


### Additional information

## Expected behavior
The message should remain displayed indefinitely, as it did in earlier Home Assistant releases, or the integration should provide a way to select the message duration.

## Actual behavior
The message disappears after approximately 60 seconds.

## Possible cause
In Home Assistant 2026.5.4, the select entity used the legacy method:
`await obj.set_lcd_text(...)`

In Home Assistant 2026.6.0, this was changed to:
`await obj.set_lcd_message_public(...)`

The public method treats an omitted resetAt value as the NVR default timeout. On this system, that default is 60 seconds.

Relevant change:
- https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/171785
- https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.5.4/homeassistant/components/unifiprotect/select.py#L164-L171
- https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.9.1/homeassistant/components/unifiprotect/select.py#L174-L185

The public API supports an explicit resetAt: null value for an indefinite message. The integration may need to pass the equivalent of reset_at=None, or expose the duration as a configurable option.

Using `action: text.set_value` on `entity_id: text.<doorbell...>` still works as expected.

query:
ViCare: hvac_action permanently `idle` on heat pumps whose compressor phase is `ready`

### The problem

On a Vitocal 150-A, `climate.*` reports `hvac_action: idle` at all times, including
while the compressor is running and the circuit is actively heating. The
`binary_sensor` for the compressor correctly reports `on` at the same moment, so the
underlying data is present and is being read successfully — it is the mapping in
`climate.py` that drops it.

The cause is the phase check added to `ViCareClimate.update()` for cooling support:

```python
for compressor in get_compressors(self._device):
    if not compressor.getActive():
        continue
    phase = None
    with suppress(PyViCareNotSupportedFeatureError):
        phase = compressor.getPhase()
    if phase == "cooling":
        cooling_active = True
    elif phase == "heating" or phase is None:
        # Phase is unset on hybrid devices that do not
        # expose it: fall back to HEATING to match the
        # pre-cooling-support behaviour.
        heating_active = True
```

My device reports `active: true` together with `phase: "ready"`. `"ready"` matches
neither branch, and it is not `None` — the feature is supported and returns a value,
just not one of the two the code anticipates. So `heating_active` is never set,
and the entity falls through to `HVACAction.IDLE`.

This is not a transient state. The `setPhase` command advertised by this device
constrains `value` to:

```json
"enum": ["off", "preparing", "not-ready", "ready"]
```

There is no `heating` or `cooling` member in that vocabulary, so on this device the
`heating` branch is unreachable by construction and `hvac_action` can only ever be
`idle`. I would expect the same for any model exposing this phase enum.

The `phase is None` fallback in the current code only catches devices where
`getPhase()` raises `PyViCareNotSupportedFeatureError`. It does not catch devices
that support the property but populate it from a different vocabulary, which is the
case here.

## Relevant feature payload

From the config entry diagnostics (device `0`, modelId `E3_Vitocal`), taken while the
unit was heating:

```json
{
  "feature": "heating.compressors.0",
  "isEnabled": true,
  "isReady": true,
  "properties": {
    "active": { "type": "boolean", "value": true },
    "phase":  { "type": "string",  "value": "ready" }
  },
  "commands": {
    "setPhase": {
      "params": {
        "value": {
          "constraints": { "enum": ["off", "preparing", "not-ready", "ready"] }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The compressor sits on the same device as `heating.circuits.0`, so
`get_compressors(self._device)` resolves it correctly — this is not a
device-association problem.

Corroborating state on the same poll:

- `heating.circuits.0.operating.modes.active` → `heating`
- `heating.circuits.0.operating.modes.heating` → `active: true`
- `heating.circuits.0.operating.programs.active` → `normalHeating`
- `heating.compressors.0.speed.current` → 20 rev/s
- `heating.compressors.0.sensors.temperature.outlet` → 42.3 °C

All four cooling programs and `heating.circuits.0.operating.modes.cooling` are
`isEnabled: false` on this installation, so there is no ambiguity about what the
compressor was doing.

## Resulting entity state

```yaml
state: auto
attributes:
  hvac_action: idle
  active_vicare_program: normalHeating
  active_vicare_mode: heating
  current_temperature: 27.9
  temperature: 20
  friendly_name: Vitocal 150A Heating
```

## Suggested fix

Treat `cooling` as the only phase that means cooling, and anything else on an active
compressor as heating:

```python
    if phase == "cooling":
        cooling_active = True
    else:
        heating_active = True
```

This keeps the cooling detection that the phase check was introduced for, and
restores the previous "active compressor means heating" behaviour for every device
that does not report a `heating`/`cooling` phase vocabulary. The guard is still
`compressor.getActive()`, so an idle compressor is unaffected either way.

An alternative, if the phase value is wanted as more than a cooling discriminator,
would be to combine it with the circuit's active mode
(`heating.circuits.N.operating.modes.active`), which reports `heating` or `cooling`
directly and is already read elsewhere in `update()`.

+"""Tests Starlink binary sensors."""
+
+from copy import deepcopy
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+
+from homeassistant.components.starlink.const import DOMAIN
+from homeassistant.const import CONF_IP_ADDRESS, STATE_OFF, STATE_UNKNOWN
+from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
+from homeassistant.util.json import JsonArrayType
+
+from .patchers import (
+    HISTORY_STATS_SUCCESS_PATCHER,
+    LOCATION_DATA_SUCCESS_PATCHER,
+    SLEEP_DATA_SUCCESS_PATCHER,
+    STATUS_DATA_FIXTURE,
+    STATUS_DATA_TARGET,
+)
+
+from tests.common import MockConfigEntry
+
+# Alerts that a dish which does not support roaming stops reporting. The
+# library builds the alert dict from the fields the dish actually sends, so
+# these keys are simply absent instead of being False.
+MISSING_ALERTS = (
+    "alert_roaming",
+    "alert_unexpected_location",
+    "alert_is_power_save_idle",
+)
+
+
+async def setup_integration(
+    hass: HomeAssistant, status_data: JsonArrayType
+) -> MockConfigEntry:

+    entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_IP_ADDRESS: "1.2.3.4:0000"})
+
+    with (
+        LOCATION_DATA_SUCCESS_PATCHER,
+        SLEEP_DATA_SUCCESS_PATCHER,
+        HISTORY_STATS_SUCCESS_PATCHER,
+        patch(STATUS_DATA_TARGET, return_value=status_data),
+    ):
+        entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+
+        await hass.config_entries.async_setup(entry.entry_id)
+        await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    return entry
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "entity_id",
+    [
+        "binary_sensor.starlink_roaming_mode",
+        "binary_sensor.starlink_unexpected_location",
+        "binary_sensor.starlink_sleep",
+    ],
+)
+async def test_alert_reported_by_dish(hass: HomeAssistant, entity_id: str) -> None:
+    """Test that an alert the dish reports is used as the state."""
+    await setup_integration(hass, deepcopy(STATUS_DATA_FIXTURE))
+
+    assert hass.states.get(entity_id).state == STATE_OFF
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "entity_id",
+    [
+        "binary_sensor.starlink_roaming_mode",
+        "binary_sensor.starlink_unexpected_location",
+        "binary_sensor.starlink_sleep",
+    ],
+)
+async def test_alert_not_reported_by_dish(hass: HomeAssistant, entity_id: str) -> None:
+    """Test that an alert the dish omits is unknown instead of raising."""
+    status_data = deepcopy(STATUS_DATA_FIXTURE)
+    for alert in MISSING_ALERTS:
+        del status_data[2][alert]
+
+    await setup_integration(hass, status_data)
+
+    assert hass.states.get(entity_id).state == STATE_UNKNOWN
+
+
+async def test_remaining_alerts_unaffected(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
+    """Test that alerts the dish still reports keep working."""
+    status_data = deepcopy(STATUS_DATA_FIXTURE)
+    for alert in MISSING_ALERTS:
+        del status_data[2][alert]
+    status_data[2]["alert_motors_stuck"] = True
+
+    await setup_integration(hass, status_data)
+
+    assert hass.states.get("binary_sensor.starlink_motors_stuck").state == "on"

I dug into this with a Shelly 2PM Gen4 configured in lift-only mode (no tilt), and found the root cause. Attribute in question: 1/258/15 = endpoint 1, cluster 0x102 (WindowCovering), attribute 0x0F (CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths). The device reports this attribute as present in its attribute set, but with value null, instead of omitting it entirely (which is what you'd expect from a lift-only covering). matter_server just persists whatever the device reports, so the stored node data ends up with "1/258/15": null. The actual bug is in how Home Assistant's Matter integration discovers cover entities: - has_attribute() (matter_server/client/models/node.py:156-178) only checks whether the attribute key exists in node_data.attributes — it does not check whether the value is null: attr_path = create_attribute_path(self.endpoint_id, cluster_id, attribute_id) return attr_path in self.node.node_data.attributes - cover.py defines four DISCOVERY_SCHEMAS (lift-only / tilt-only / neither / both), each keyed on has_attribute/absent_attributes for CurrentPositionLiftPercent100ths and CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths. - Because the tilt attribute key is technically "present" (even though null), the lift-only schema doesn't match (its absent_attributes check on tilt fails). - The lift+tilt schema's required_attributes check does pass (both keys exist) — but then discovery.py:152-157 runs this check: `#` check if PRIMARY value exists but is none/null if not schema.allow_none_value and any( endpoint.get_attribute_value(None, val_schema) in (None, NullValue) for val_schema in schema.required_attributes ): continue - Since CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths evaluates to None, and allow_none_value defaults to False, this schema is skipped too. Net result: none of the four cover discovery schemas match, so no cover entity is created at all for lift-only devices that report the tilt attribute as present-but-null instead of omitting it. Fix that worked for me: add allow_none_value=True to the MatterCoverPositionAwareLiftAndTilt schema in homeassistant/components/matter/cover.py. This lets the schema match despite the null tilt value; the entity then correctly reports current_cover_tilt_position = None and (since the device's AcceptedCommandList doesn't include GoToTiltPercentage) never exposes SET_TILT_POSITION, so no dummy tilt control shows up — just a working lift-only cover. A more targeted upstream fix might be to treat a present-but-null optional/s Jump to bottom (ctrl+End) ↓ for schema-matching purposes, rather than broadly loosening allow_none_value, but this reproduces and resolves the issue for me. I have the same issue. I can confirm this is not an isolated case, and my testing supports @martin3000's finding about the tilt attribute being the trigger — with a caveat worth documenting. **Same symptom:** Shelly 2PM Gen4 in cover profile, paired via Matter, on Home Assistant 2026.8.2. Diagnostics for the device show the WindowCovering cluster (0x0102 / 258) correctly interviewed on endpoint 1, with device type 514 (Window Covering Device) and lift attributes populated: ```json "1/29/0":[{"0":514,"1":1}], "1/29/1":[3,4,29,258], "1/258/0":0, "1/258/7":13, "1/258/8":0, "1/258/9":null, "1/258/10":0, "1/258/11":6, "1/258/12":null, "1/258/13":0, "1/258/14":6, "1/258/15":null, "1/258/23":1, "1/258/26":0, "1/258/65531":[0,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15,23,26,...] ``` Attributes 9/12/15 (CurrentPositionTiltPercentage, TargetPositionTiltPercent100ths, CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths) are `null`. I verified this is the device's genuine, stable value — not a stale/cached artifact — by: power-cycling the physical Shelly, then explicitly triggering a fresh `interview_node` against `python-matter-server`'s own websocket API. After that clean re-interview, all three tilt attributes were still reported as `null`. So this is consistently how this device (lift-only, no slat/tilt hardware) reports itself over Matter. As a result, `python-matter-server` reports the endpoint correctly, but Home Assistant only ever creates a disabled-by-default `sensor.*` for the target lift position — never a `cover.*` entity. No controls. **Partial repro of the fix:** Editing `python-matter-server`'s storage JSON directly to set attributes 9/12/15 from `null` to `0` for this node, then restarting matter-server and reloading/restarting Home Assistant, *does* cause HA to create a `cover.*` registry entry that never existed before — confirming a null tilt attribute is what gates entity creation for this endpoint/device-type combination in HA's Matter integration. However, the resulting `cover.*` entity in my case stayed permanently `unavailable` (`restored: true`) even after a full Home Assistant restart, while other entities on the same device (e.g. the config-status binary_sensor) came back with live state normally. My guess is that `python-matter-server`'s live subscription re-reports the device's real (null) value shortly after reconnecting, which HA's entity then can't handle gracefully — so a storage-only edit gets a registry entry created but never wired up to a working live state. I could not get it into a genuinely functional state without also patching the value persistently faster than the live subscription overwrites it, which isn't practical outside of a debugging session like this. **Summary of what's now confirmed:** - The WindowCovering endpoint is correctly reported by python-matter-server, with `null` tilt attributes on a real lift-only device — confirmed via a clean re-interview after a physical power cycle, not just a stale cache. - A `null` tilt attribute appears to prevent Home Assistant's Matter integration from creating a `cover` entity for the endpoint at all; only out-of-band edits that make it non-null trigger entity creation. - Even once created, the entity does not reliably reach a live/working state, likely because the live subscription reports the same null value back. This points at the entity-mapping/availability logic for the Matter `WindowCovering` cluster incorrectly treating a legitimately-null optional tilt attribute as a reason to skip the `cover` entity for lift-only devices, rather than falling back to lift-only support (which the same endpoint reports correctly). Update: I have a clean, fully-verified confirmation now — no storage edits involved this time. I went back to the same Shelly 2PM Gen4 (lift-only shutter) and, purely for testing, enabled the Slat/Tilt control in the Shelly app (even though the physical shutter has no slats) and drove it to 99% lift / 87% tilt from the Shelly app. That produced genuine, device-reported non-null values for the Matter tilt attributes: ```json "1/258/9": 13, // CurrentPositionTiltPercentage (deprecated) "1/258/12": 1338, // TargetPositionTiltPercent100ths "1/258/15": 1338 // CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths ``` (values appear inverted vs. the app's 87% — likely an open/closed convention difference, not relevant here) After a full Home Assistant restart with these real, non-manipulated values present, HA created **and correctly live-wired** the `cover.*` entity for the first time — no manual storage patching needed: ```json {"state": "open", "current_position": 100, "current_tilt_position": 87, "device_class": "blind", "supported_features": 143} ``` This cleanly confirms the root cause without any out-of-band editing: **a `null` value on the Matter WindowCovering tilt attributes (9/12/15) prevents Home Assistant's Matter integration from creating a working `cover` entity at all — even though the device's own FeatureMap (`1/258/65532` = `5`, i.e. Lift + PositionAwareLift only, no Tilt/PositionAwareTilt bits) correctly declares that tilt is not supported.** So there are two separate issues layered here: 1. **Shelly-side (likely a Matter conformance issue):** the tilt attributes (9/12/15) are listed in the endpoint's `AttributeList` (`1/258/65531`) as supported even though the FeatureMap doesn't set the Tilt/PositionAwareTilt bits — per the Matter spec these attributes are conformance-gated on those feature bits and shouldn't appear in `AttributeList` at all for a lift-only device. Interestingly, other Matter controllers (I tested Apple Home) handle this gracefully and expose lift-only control regardless — so the null values alone don't have to break interoperability if the client is defensive about it. 2. **Home Assistant-side:** the Matter integration's entity-mapping logic for `WindowCovering` appears to require a non-null tilt attribute value to construct a working `cover` entity, rather than gracefully falling back to lift-only control when tilt attributes are declared-but-unpopulated. Given other controllers cope fine with the same non-conformant data, this looks like the more actionable fix, regardless of whether Shelly also fixes their attribute list. For this reason you can set "allow_none_value=True" in cover.py ``` MatterDiscoverySchema( platform=Platform.COVER, entity_description=MatterCoverEntityDescription( key="MatterCoverPositionAwareLiftAndTilt", name=None ), entity_class=MatterCover, required_attributes=( clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.OperationalStatus, clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.Type, clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.CurrentPositionLiftPercent100ths, clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths, ), # Some devices (e.g. Shelly 2PM Gen4 in lift-only mode) report # CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths as present but null instead of # omitting it entirely. Without this, no cover schema matches at all. allow_none_value=True, ), ``` That looks like the right fix to me. Other Matter controllers (I checked Apple Home) already treat a present-but-null tilt attribute as "no tilt" rather than bailing out, so `allow_none_value=True` here would bring HA's behavior in line with how other ecosystems already handle this non-conformant-but-common device pattern. **Update:** I reached out to Shelly support directly with the analysis from this thread (null-but-present tilt attributes on lift-only devices, `AttributeList` vs. `FeatureMap` mismatch, and the fact that other Matter controllers like Apple Home handle it gracefully). Their response: they don't see any action needed on their end. Their reasoning is that they can't provide individual support for every smart home platform, and other Matter-capable systems (they specifically mentioned Apple HomeKit) recognize the Shelly cover devices over Matter without issue. So from Shelly's side, no fix is planned for the `AttributeList`/`FeatureMap` conformance mismatch. That means the practical path forward is squarely on the Home Assistant side — i.e. the `allow_none_value=True` fix @martin3000 proposed above, which already matches how other ecosystems (Apple Home) cope with this same non-conformant-but-common device behavior. Flagging this so it doesn't stall waiting on a device-side fix that isn't coming — happy to help verify a PR against my Shelly 2PM Gen4 if that's useful. In the past, I have occasionally fixed bugs in Home Assistant. This particular fix would only require about two minutes of code changes. However, the rest of the effort required to submit a PR is immense. Tests have to be written and run, the test results have to be submitted, and there are apparently quite a few other steps involved. I don't know all the requirements, and the overall effort is simply too much for me. On top of that, the people reviewing PRs are not exactly friendly. You don't really feel like someone who is contributing and trying to help; rather, you feel like you're getting in the way. So I won't be submitting a PR for this fix. diff --git a/homeassistant/components/matter/cover.py b/homeassistant/components/matter/cover.py
index 5fe0995ff46..afc55ba7101 100644
--- a/homeassistant/components/matter/cover.py
+++ b/homeassistant/components/matter/cover.py
@@ -174,9 +174,10 @@ class MatterCover(MatterEntity, CoverEntity):
                 self.current_cover_position,
             )
 
-        if self._entity_info.endpoint.has_attribute(
+        has_tilt_position_attribute = self._entity_info.endpoint.has_attribute(
             None, clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths
-        ):
+        )
+        if has_tilt_position_attribute:
             # current tilt position is inverted in matter (100 is closed, 0 is open)
             current_cover_tilt_position = self.get_matter_attribute_value(
                 clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths
@@ -206,9 +207,17 @@ class MatterCover(MatterEntity, CoverEntity):
         commands = self.get_matter_attribute_value(
             clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.AcceptedCommandList
         )
+        feature_map = self.get_matter_attribute_value(
+            clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.FeatureMap
+        )
         if clusters.WindowCovering.Commands.GoToLiftPercentage.command_id in commands:
             supported_features |= CoverEntityFeature.SET_POSITION
-        if clusters.WindowCovering.Commands.GoToTiltPercentage.command_id in commands:
+        # Some devices report GoToTiltPercentage in AcceptedCommandList even
+        # without tilt support, so also require the FeatureMap Tilt bit.
+        if (
+            clusters.WindowCovering.Commands.GoToTiltPercentage.command_id in commands
+            and feature_map & clusters.WindowCovering.Bitmaps.Feature.kTilt
+        ):
             supported_features |= CoverEntityFeature.SET_TILT_POSITION
         self._attr_supported_features = supported_features
 
@@ -271,6 +280,11 @@ DISCOVERY_SCHEMAS = [
             clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.OperationalStatus,
             clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.Type,
             clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.CurrentPositionLiftPercent100ths,
+        ),
+        # tilt is optional, not required: some devices (e.g. Shelly 2PM Gen4)
+        # report it as present but null instead of omitting it when tilt is
+        # disabled, which would otherwise fail schema matching
+        optional_attributes=(
             clusters.WindowCovering.Attributes.CurrentPositionTiltPercent100ths,
         ),
     ),

query:
Fix swallowed exceptions in mochad action handlers

The `mochad` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `light.py`, `switch.py`:**
- `turn_off` (light.py)
- `turn_on` (light.py)
- `turn_off` (switch.py)
- `turn_on` (switch.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

Part of home-assistant/epics#64
