Alexa: every temperature command switches a Nest thermostat to heat_cool, because TurnOn maps to the default climate turn_on which picks HEAT_COOL

# The problem

Any Alexa temperature command sent through the cloud Alexa integration ("set it to 77", "raise it two degrees", "lower it one degree") changes the thermostat's HVAC mode from `cool` to `heat_cool` and the requested setpoint is lost.

Cause, captured on the wire with `google_nest_sdm.auth` at debug:

```
22:41:33.648 request[post json]={'command': 'sdm.devices.commands.ThermostatMode.SetMode', 'params': {'mode': 'HEATCOOL'}}
22:41:33.761 [homeassistant.components.climate] Check valid temperature 25 C (77 F) in range 10 C - 32 C
22:41:33.761 request[post json]={'command': 'sdm.devices.commands.ThermostatTemperatureSetpoint.SetCool', 'params': {'coolCelsius': 25.0}}
```

The SetMode arrives 113 ms before the climate service's own validation line, so it is not part of `set_temperature`. It is a separate directive: Alexa sends `Alexa.PowerController.TurnOn` ahead of the setpoint, as it does for any endpoint that reports a PowerController.

Three pieces combine:

1. `alexa/entities.py` `ClimateCapabilities` yields `AlexaPowerController` when the climate entity supports `TURN_ON | TURN_OFF`. The `nest` integration sets both unconditionally in `_get_supported_features`.
2. Alexa therefore sends `TurnOn` before `SetTargetTemperature` / `AdjustTargetTemperature`. HA maps that to `climate.turn_on`.
3. `ClimateEntity.async_turn_on` (the "Fake turn on" default in `climate/__init__.py`) iterates `(HEAT_COOL, HEAT, COOL)` and sets the first one the entity supports. `nest` does not override `turn_on`. So "turn on" on a thermostat that is already on and in `cool` means "switch to heat_cool".

Result: the mode flips to `heat_cool`, and the `SetCool` that follows 113 ms later is rejected by the SDM API because the device is no longer in COOL mode. The user's setpoint never lands.

Reproduces with no Alexa involved: call `climate.turn_on` on a Nest that is in `cool`. It switches to `heat_cool`.

# What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.0

# What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Unknown. Thermostat was added to this instance on 2026-09-09.

# What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS (HAOS 18.2)

# Integration causing the issue

alexa (cloud), climate, nest

# Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/alexa.smart_home/
https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/nest/

# Diagnostics information

Not attached. The relevant evidence is the log excerpt above; the nest diagnostics carry the SDM project and device identifiers.

# Example YAML snippet

None needed. Default `nest` config flow, default cloud Alexa exposure of a `climate` entity.

# Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

State history of the entity for one "set it to 77" (local time):

```
22:41:33  cool       target 77          <- SetTargetTemperature applied
22:41:34  heat_cool  range 68 / 77      <- TurnOn had already switched the mode; device reports HEATCOOL
```

Logbook attributes the `heat_cool` row to the Cloud system user.

# Additional information

Thermostat: Nest Learning Thermostat (4th gen) via the `nest` SDM integration. `hvac_modes` reports `heat, cool, heat_cool, off`; `supported_features` is 411 (TARGET_TEMPERATURE, TARGET_TEMPERATURE_RANGE, FAN_MODE, PRESET_MODE, TURN_OFF, TURN_ON).

Suggested fixes, any one of which breaks the chain:

- `ClimateEntity.async_turn_on` default: if the entity is already in a mode other than `off`, do nothing (or restore the last active mode), instead of jumping to HEAT_COOL.
- `nest`: override `async_turn_on` to restore the previous mode rather than falling into the default.
- `alexa`: for climate entities, treat `TurnOn` as a no-op when `hvac_mode != off`.

Workarounds tried and rejected: an automation that reverts the mode on a Cloud-user `heat_cool` change (the setpoint is already lost by then), and a mode-only revert (same). The working workaround was to link the thermostat to Alexa natively over Matter and hide the HA entity from Alexa.

### The problem

query:
samsungtv: 2016 K‑series that need encrypted pairing can't be added (no websocket→encrypted fallback)

### The problem

## Summary

My older Samsung smart TV (tizen based) used to work with this integration, but at some point stopped working. Disclosure: have been using claude to help diagnose and troubleshoot.

Context: A 2016 Tizen **K‑series** TV that requires the **encrypted / CloudPINPage** pairing method
cannot be added through the config flow. HA's method selection commits to the **websocket
(token)** method for it and there is **no fallback** to the encrypted method, so the flow
dead‑ends at `cannot_connect`.

Concretely: **UN55KU6290** (`modelName: UN55KU6290`, `model: 16_JAZZL_UHD_BASIC`,
`msfVersion: 2.1.0`, **no `TokenAuthSupport`**).

- REST `/api/v2/` device info is fetched fine on 8002 → `async_get_device_info()` selects
  `METHOD_WEBSOCKET`.
- The token handshake on 8002 returns `ms.channel.timeOut` (no on‑screen "Allow?" popup,
  because the set advertises no `TokenAuthSupport`). In `SamsungTVWSBridge.async_try_connect()`
  this surfaces as `AsyncioTimeoutError`/`ConnectionFailure` → `RESULT_CANNOT_CONNECT`.
- `config_flow` aborts (`RESULT_CANNOT_CONNECT` → `AbortFlow`). The encrypted method that
  would work is never attempted.

**The library is not the problem here.** Driving [samsungtvws](https://github.com/xchwarze/samsung-tv-ws-api/) (3.0.5) directly against this
TV, the encrypted CloudPINPage flow completes end‑to‑end (PIN on screen → token + session_id;
control on port 8000). This is purely a method‑selection gap in the homeassistant samsungtv integration.

## Why the obvious heuristics are unsafe

The encrypted probe is gated by `model_requires_encryption()` = `model[4] in ("H","J")`,
introduced in #71291 to fix #70708 and **#70708's TV was itself a K‑series, UE32K5600**
(`model: 16_HAWKM_FHD`, `msfVersion: 2.1.0`), which must use **websocket** (the encrypted
bridge broke its power‑off). Its REST device info **also has no `TokenAuthSupport`**.

So among 2016 K‑series sets with identical‑looking REST info (`msfVersion 2.1.0`, no
`TokenAuthSupport`):

| Model | REST `TokenAuthSupport` | Correct method |
|---|---|---|
| UN55KU6290 | absent | **encrypted** |
| UE32K5600 (#70708) | absent | **websocket** |

Therefore:
- **Appending `"K"` to the letter list** would re‑break UE32K5600 (regress #70708).
- **Keying on `TokenAuthSupport` absence** would do the same; and since UE32K5600 evidently
  responds on port 8000 (it previously paired as an encrypted bridge), the existing
  `RESULT_CANNOT_CONNECT` fall‑through wouldn't save it.

The only signal that reliably separates the two is **whether the websocket/token attempt
actually succeeds**. That's observable at pairing time: UN55KU6290 → `RESULT_CANNOT_CONNECT`;
UE32K5600 → `RESULT_AUTH_MISSING`/`RESULT_SUCCESS`.

## Proposed direction (seeking maintainer preference before coding)

**A. Automatic fallback (default path).** When the initial websocket pairing attempt fails
with `RESULT_CANNOT_CONNECT` (i.e. genuinely can't establish the token channel — *not*
`RESULT_AUTH_MISSING`, which just means the popup is pending), fall back to probing/pairing
the encrypted bridge before aborting. This only affects the existing failure path, so it
can't regress UE32K5600/#70708 (they never return `CANNOT_CONNECT` there) or modern token
sets. The H/J discovery gate stays as‑is.

Open questions:
1. Preferred location/shape: a fallback inside `async_step_pairing`, or restructure
   `async_get_device_info`?
2. Trigger scope — `CANNOT_CONNECT` only, or also `NOT_SUPPORTED`? I want to be conservative
   and not misclassify "auth popup pending."
3. The reauth path notes "on websocket we will get RESULT_CANNOT_CONNECT when auth is
   missing"; I'd scope A to the *initial* add flow to avoid that ambiguity. Agree?

**B. Optional manual override (opt‑in, additive).** Add an optional
`authentication_method` selector to the user step, default **`automatic`** (current behavior,
unchanged byte‑for‑byte). Power users could force `websocket` / `encrypted` / `legacy` for the
long tail of models auto‑detection can't classify.

Open questions:
1. Is an explicit method override acceptable for a gold‑tier integration, or is auto‑only preferred?
2. If acceptable, would you want it behind advanced options
   (`self.show_advanced_options`)? (No samsungtv precedent for that today.)

Happy to open a PR for whichever combination you prefer. Test plan includes a new
`device_info_UN55KU6290.json` fixture plus regression coverage asserting UE32K5600‑style
websocket sets stay on the websocket method.

## Environment
- Home Assistant Core: `dev`
- Device: Samsung UN55KU6290 (2016, Tizen). Reproduced end‑to‑end; encrypted method verified
  working via direct `samsungtvws` 3.0.5.


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

 2026.7.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.5.0

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

samsungtv

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/samsungtv

### Diagnostics information

```txt
The diagnostic sequence: REST info is fetched on 8002 (note `modelName: UN55KU6290`,
`model: 16_JAZZL_UHD_BASIC`, **no `TokenAuthSupport`**), the model check declines the
encrypted path, and the websocket/token attempt then times out on both ports →
`RESULT_CANNOT_CONNECT`. Relevant emitters (`homeassistant/components/samsungtv/bridge.py`):
```

query:
Alexa Event Gateway HTTP 204 No Content causes unhandled JSONDecodeError in state_report.py

### The problem

When Home Assistant sends proactive event notifications to Amazon's Alexa Event Gateway (such as `DoorbellPress` for entities configured with `display_categories: DOORBELL` or `ChangeReport`), the background task crashes with an unhandled exception:

`orjson.JSONDecodeError: Input is a zero-length, empty document: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`

This issue began occurring suddenly on **September 7, 2026**, without any changes to our Home Assistant configuration or recent code modifications in `state_report.py` (which was last touched in Core around August 5).

The root cause is an **upstream API change by Amazon**: Amazon's Alexa Event Gateway (`https://api.eu.amazonalexa.com/v3/events`) has started responding with `HTTP 204 No Content` for accepted proactive events instead of `HTTP 202 Accepted`.

Because `state_report.py` strictly checks `if response.status == HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED:`, Home Assistant assumes that any non-202 status code is an error and immediately tries to deserialize the response body as JSON via `json_loads_object(response_text)`. Since an `HTTP 204` response has an empty body (`""`), `orjson` crashes on the empty document.

The event is actually delivered and processed successfully by Alexa (e.g. Echo devices announce the doorbell), but Home Assistant crashes the task and logs an error on every single trigger.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

alexa

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/alexa/

### Diagnostics information

N/A (YAML integration without UI config flow)

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
alexa:
  smart_home:
    locale: es-ES
    endpoint: https://api.eu.amazonalexa.com/v3/events
    client_id: !secret alexa_client_id
    client_secret: !secret alexa_client_secret
    filter:
      include_entities:
        - binary_sensor.doorbell
    entity_config:
      binary_sensor.doorbell:
        display_categories: DOORBELL
```

```txt
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant] Error doing job: Task exception was never retrieved (task: None)

  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/alexa/state_report.py", line 355, in _async_entity_state_listener
    await async_send_doorbell_event_message(
        hass, smart_home_config, alexa_changed_entity
    )
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/alexa/state_report.py", line 598, in async_send_doorbell_event_message
    response_json = json_loads_object(response_text)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/util/json.py", line 54, in json_loads_object
    value: JsonValueType = json_loads(obj)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/util/json.py", line 40, in json_loads
    return orjson.loads(obj)
orjson.JSONDecodeError: Input is a zero-length, empty document: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

### Additional information

### Technical Details
In `homeassistant/components/alexa/state_report.py`, Home Assistant only accepts `202 Accepted`:
```python
if response.status == HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED:  # 202
    return
```
When Amazon responds with `HTTP 204 No Content`, Home Assistant enters the error handling branch and executes:
```python
response_json = json_loads_object(response_text)
```
Because `response_text` is `""`, `orjson` crashes with an unhandled exception.

A direct API call to Amazon's Event Gateway (`https://api.eu.amazonalexa.com/v3/events`) with a valid `DoorbellPress` payload confirms that Amazon returns status code `204` with a body length of 0.

### Proposed Solution
1. Treat `HTTPStatus.NO_CONTENT` (204) and `HTTPStatus.OK` (200) as success alongside `HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED` (202) in both `async_send_doorbell_event_message` and `async_send_changereport_message`.
2. Guard `json_loads_object` defensively so that unexpected empty responses on real errors log the HTTP status code rather than crashing with an unhandled task exception.

```diff
@@ -438,4 +438,10 @@ async def async_send_changereport_message(

+    try:

+        response_payload = cast(JsonObjectType, response_json.get("payload", {}))
+    except Exception:

-    response_json = json_loads_object(response_text)
-    response_payload = cast(JsonObjectType, response_json["payload"])
+    try:
+        response_json = json_loads_object(response_text) if response_text else {}
+        response_payload = cast(JsonObjectType, response_json.get("payload", {}))
+        _LOGGER.error(
+            "Error when sending DoorbellPress event for %s to Alexa (status %s): %s: %s",
+            alexa_entity.entity_id,
```

query:
Backup encrypt/decrypt rewrite skips supervisor.tar, breaking mount restore

cc @agners @mdegat01, you reviewed and merged home-assistant/supervisor#6411.

## Context

Since Supervisor 2026.03.3 (home-assistant/supervisor#6411 and #6674), backups contain `supervisor.tar(.gz)` with the network storage mount and Docker registry config. It is encrypted like the other inner tars. On my dad's system the network storage was gone after restoring a backup. The primary cause is a Supervisor bug, home-assistant/supervisor#7213, but Core has a second one that would still break the same restore after that fix.

## Problem

`_decrypt_backup` and `_encrypt_backup` in `homeassistant/components/backup/util.py` only process inner tars whose prefix is in `_get_expected_archives()`, which is `homeassistant`, the addon slugs and the folders. `supervisor.tar.gz` is not in that set, so it is copied through unchanged while `protected` in `backup.json` is flipped. This happens whenever Core rewrites a backup: uploading to hassio locations with mixed encryption settings in `_async_upload_backup`, or a decrypted download.

Supervisor then opens the tar based on the backup metadata and fails, reproduced with securetar 2026.4.1:

| Rewritten by Core | Inner tar state | Supervisor restore | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| decrypted | still encrypted | no password | `tarfile.ReadError: not a gzip file` |
| encrypted | still plain | with password | `SecureTarReadError: The inner tar is not gzip or tar, wrong key?` |

Both are swallowed by `restore_supervisor_config` and the mounts are silently not restored.

## Fix

Add `supervisor` to the expected archives, or process every `*.tar` / `*.tar.gz` member the same way. `validate_password_stream` already treats any inner tar as encrypted.
hints:
Uh, nice find! I was not aware that Core mangles the backup with a fixed tarball list 😢 

If we want to stick with the fixed list, we should add a comment on Supervisor side so this won't happen again.

The fixed list got introduced with #144495 by @emontnemery, given the rational of that PR I guess we want to keep the fixed list.

Tested your fork (https://github.com/DieEneSchrodinger/energyflip-client/commit/7cce43e9) against 3 real EnergyFlip accounts. The new endpoints (actualsSummary + cumulativeHistory) are the right approach — good find.
  With two small fixes it works fully.

##  Bug 1 — _customer_id never gets set when used with Home Assistant

  The HA huisbaasje integration calls energyflip.authenticate() in async_setup_entry before calling current_measurements(). So when current_measurements() runs, is_authenticated() is already True and the if not
  self.is_authenticated() block — which is where customer_overview() is called — gets skipped entirely. _customer_id stays None, and every subsequent URL becomes .../customers/None/....

  Fix: check _customer_id independently:

  if not self.is_authenticated():
      await self.authenticate()
  if self._customer_id is None:   # also covers re-auth via invalidate_authentication()
      await self.customer_overview()

## Bug 2 — wrong types for "no data" fallbacks

Two places return non-dict values where the HA coordinator expects {"value": ..., "cost": ...} dicts:

coordinator does current_measurements[source_type]["thisDay"]["value"]
so the fallback must be a dict, not an int:
measurements[type]["this" + period.capitalize()] = 0          # ❌ int
measurements[type]["this" + period.capitalize()] = {"value": 0, "cost": 0}  # ✓

coordinator checks `is not None` then does ["rate"] — string "None" passes the check:
measurements[type]["measurement"] = "None"   # ❌ str
measurements[type]["measurement"] = None     # ✓

Result after both fixes: all 3 accounts recovered, config entries show loaded, gas_today / current_power sensors report live values again.

One note: some source types from the old API (electricityOutLow, electricityOutHigh, etc.) are not present in the v4 cumulativeHistory aggregations response, so those sensors stay unavailable. That may just be how the  v4 API works for meters without production/export — not a bug in your code.

I made changes to fix the bugs you addressed. In terms of the v4 API, as stated in a previous message, it no longer supports separate current measurements for electricityOutLow, electricityOutHigh, etc. 
I don't expect to be able to find new endpoints that support these measurements so I will probably remove them from the Home Assistant intergration when I make my PR.

Spotify reauthentication fails with KeyError: 'id' when OAuth refresh token becomes invalid

### The problem

When a Spotify OAuth refresh token becomes invalid, Home Assistant correctly detects that reauthentication is required. However, the Spotify reauthentication flow crashes before the reauthentication dialog can be shown.

The following exception occurs:

KeyError: 'id'

The error originates from:

description_placeholders={"account": reauth_entry.data["id"]}

in homeassistant/components/spotify/config_flow.py.

My Spotify config entries do not contain an id field inside data. The Spotify user ID is stored as the config entry's unique_id instead.

I have three Spotify accounts configured using the same Spotify authentication implementation. Two accounts currently have invalid/expired refresh tokens and both produce this error. The third account still refreshes successfully and therefore does not enter the reauthentication flow.

The affected config entries have a structure like this (tokens and IDs removed):

{

Bosch SHC: Shutter Control devices received by boschshcpy but no cover entities are created

### The problem

I have a Bosch Smart Home Controller II with 5 Bosch Zigbee roller shutter devices.

The Bosch SHC integration itself is configured successfully in Home Assistant and the controller is shown as a device. However, none of the 5 roller shutters appear as devices or cover entities in Home Assistant.

All 5 roller shutters work correctly in the Bosch Smart Home app.

Reloading the Bosch SHC integration and restarting Home Assistant does not change the behavior.

I enabled debug logging for the Bosch SHC integration and reproduced the issue by moving the shutters.

The debug log shows that boschshcpy successfully discovers/refreshes 5 devices:

"Poll-id resubscribed — refreshing 5 device(s) via short-poll"

It also receives live ShutterControl events from the Zigbee shutter devices, including:

- level
- operationState (MOVING / STOPPED)
- calibration information
- reference moving times

PowerMeter updates from the shutter devices are received as well.

There are no ENTITY_NOT_FOUND or 404 errors in my debug log.

Despite boschshcpy clearly receiving the ShutterControl services and live state changes, Home Assistant only creates the SmartHomeController device. No cover entities are created.

According to the Bosch SHC integration documentation, cover entities should be created for each Shutter Control device.

This looks similar to #148867, but the important difference is that my setup does NOT produce the 404 / ENTITY_NOT_FOUND errors reported there. Communication with the shutter devices appears to work correctly.

core-2026.9.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Unknown / never worked on this installation

@phreak2010 Found it — this is a real gap in the version of `bosch_shc` bundled with Core, not a config/hardware issue on your end.

Your 5 shutters are Zigbee micromodule-based (the PowerMeter events in your log are the giveaway — that's only wired up for the micromodule shutter variant). Core's `cover.py` only ever creates entities for the `BBL` device bucket (Bosch's own wired shutter relay); it never got extended to also cover `MICROMODULE_SHUTTER`/blinds, even though the underlying `boschshcpy` library (already pinned in Core) has supported that device type for a long time. So boschshcpy discovers and polls your devices fine — Core's integration just never asks it for them.

This has already been fixed in the actively-maintained HACS version of this integration, which stays ahead of what's bundled in Core:

**https://github.com/tschamm/boschshc-hass**

To use it while a Core fix is prepared:
1. Install [HACS](https://hacs.xyz) if you don't have it already.
2. In HA: **HACS → Integrations → search "Bosch SHC" → Install**, then restart Home Assistant.
3. Your existing config entry keeps working as-is — a `custom_components/bosch_shc/` install takes priority over Core's bundled version of the same integration, no need to remove/re-add anything.
4. Full instructions: https://github.com/tschamm/boschshc-hass#installation

We'll also prepare a PR to port this into Core.

query:
xiaomi_ble: KeyError for ExtendedBinarySensorDeviceClass.STABILIZED on every Mi Body Composition Scale 2 advertisement

### Environment

- Home Assistant **2026.9.2** (Home Assistant OS)
- Integration: built-in `xiaomi_ble`
- Device: **Xiaomi Mi Body Composition Scale 2** (XMTZC05HM), advertised name `MIBFS`, MAC `0C:95:41:B6:A2:68`
- BLE received by the HA host directly (RSSI −60…−70), no proxy/ESPHome involved

### What happens

Every advertisement from the scale produces an ERROR with a traceback:

```
2026-09-15 13:08:26.711 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.xiaomi_ble] Unexpected error updating MIBFS data
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/bluetooth/passive_update_processor.py", line 608, in async_handle_update
    new_data = self.update_method(update)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/xiaomi_ble/binary_sensor.py", line 120, in sensor_update_to_bluetooth_data_update
    device_key_to_bluetooth_entity_key(device_key): BINARY_SENSOR_DESCRIPTIONS[
                                                    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        description.device_class
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    ]
    ^
KeyError: <ExtendedBinarySensorDeviceClass.STABILIZED: 'stabilized'>
```

Counts from two weigh-ins (each weigh-in is a burst of advertisements while the user stands on the scale):

| when | errors |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-14 22:42 | 1 |
| 2026-09-14 22:44 (weigh-in) | 46 |
| 2026-09-15 06:15–06:16 | 4 |
| 2026-09-15 13:08 (weigh-in) | 15 |

The logger name alternates between the advertised name and the MAC (`Unexpected error updating MIBFS data` / `Unexpected error updating 0C:95:41:B6:A2:68 data`).

### Cause

The `xiaomi_ble` library emits a `STABILIZED` binary sensor on **every** scale-v2 packet — both when the reading is stable and when it is not (`site-packages/xiaomi_ble/parser.py`, `_parse_scale_v2`):

```python
mass_stabilized = bool(int(control_byte & (1 << 5)))
...
if mass_stabilized and not mass_removed and mass > 0:
    self.update_predefined_sensor(SensorLibrary.MASS__MASS_KILOGRAMS, mass)
    self.update_binary_sensor(key=ExtendedBinarySensorDeviceClass.STABILIZED, ...)   # True
else:
    if mass > 0:
        self.update_binary_sensor(key=ExtendedBinarySensorDeviceClass.STABILIZED, ...)   # False
```

HA then looks the description up by `device_class` in `BINARY_SENSOR_DESCRIPTIONS`, but that dict has entries for `XiaomiBinarySensorDeviceClass.*` and for a set of `ExtendedBinarySensorDeviceClass.*` values (`ANTILOCK`, `ARMED`, `CHILDLOCK`, `DEVICE_FORCIBLY_REMOVED`, `DOOR_LEFT_OPEN`, `DOOR_STUCK`, `FINGERPRINT`, `KNOCK_ON_THE_DOOR`, `PRY_THE_DOOR`, `TOOTHBRUSH`) — **`STABILIZED` is missing**. Hence the `KeyError` on every packet.

### Impact

1. Log spam — one full traceback per BLE advertisement, i.e. dozens per weighing.
2. The stabilization binary sensor entity is **never created**, so the signal is unusable by anything downstream. Concretely: `bodymiscale` has an optional "stabilization sensor" config field that expects exactly this entity; with it unavailable, users of this scale can only rely on the raw weight/impedance state events, which is what makes measurement-cycle ordering bugs possible (see dckiller51/bodymiscale — a fix here is a prerequisite for that integration's intended flow).
3. `sensor.*_weight` / `*_impedance` are **not** affected — they go through the separate `sensor.py` processor, and they do keep updating during the same error bursts (verified: the stabilized weight was written at 22:44:36 while errors were still being logged).

### Suggested fix

Add the missing description, e.g.:

```python
ExtendedBinarySensorDeviceClass.STABILIZED: BinarySensorEntityDescription(
    key=ExtendedBinarySensorDeviceClass.STABILIZED,
),
```

(no `device_class` mapping needed, same style as `ANTILOCK`/`CHILDLOCK`). Alternatively, skip binary sensor descriptions whose `device_class` is not in `BINARY_SENSOR_DESCRIPTIONS` so an unknown class can never take down the whole update.

Almost one year and still not fixed :').

I can reproduce this on HA 2026.9.2 / pyheos 1.0.6 with three real HEOS devices (two AVRs and a speaker), and the cause looks like it is in the integration rather than in the card.

`HeosMediaPlayer.async_join_players()` builds the member list as "self + the entities passed in" and then calls `heos.set_group(player_ids)`. In the HEOS protocol `set_group` *replaces* the group with exactly the players given, so any existing member that is not passed in again is dropped.

Cards that let you add speakers one at a time (Maxi Media Player among them) call `join` with only the newly selected player. The first call creates a group of two, the second call replaces it with leader + the new player, which silently kicks the previously grouped player out. That matches the reported "it disconnect one group everytime".

Test on real hardware, all three players idle:

1. `join` on player A with `group_members: [B]` → group is A + B.
2. `join` on player A with `group_members: [C]` → group is A + C; **B has been removed.**
3. `join` on player A with `group_members: [B, C]` → group is A + B + C, as expected.
4. `unjoin` on A → group dissolved.

Nothing was logged in any of these steps.

**Workaround for users:** call `media_player.join` once with the complete list of members instead of adding them one by one.

For comparison, Sonos adds the given members to the existing group instead of replacing it, so the same card works there. If maintainers agree that `join` should be additive, the fix is to merge the requested members with the current group membership (available in `coordinator.heos.groups`) before calling `set_group`. Happy to open a PR for that.

*(Diagnosis and the hardware test above were done together with Claude Code, which also read the integration source and proposed the additive fix.)*

query:
Fix swallowed exceptions in kodi action handlers

The `kodi` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `notify.py`:**
- `async_send_message` (notify.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

query:
Tuya fan: set_percentage(0) doesn't turn off enum-speed fans (snaps to lowest speed), turn_off works fine

### The problem

## The problem

When a Tuya fan entity only exposes a small number of discrete speed steps (an `Enum`-type `fan_speed` DP rather than a continuous range), turning the fan off via the speed slider/dial (which calls `fan.set_percentage` with `percentage: 0`) does **not** turn the fan off. Instead, it leaves the fan **on** and snaps to the lowest available speed step. The dedicated on/off toggle (`fan.turn_off`) works correctly — the bug is isolated to the `percentage: 0` code path.

## Reproduction steps

1. Have a Tuya fan device whose speed is Tuya DP `fan_speed`, an `Enum` with a small fixed range (e.g. `["1", "2", "3"]` → HA percentage steps 33/67/100%).
2. Turn the fan on at any speed, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   service: fan.turn_on
   target:
     entity_id: fan.example_fan
   data:
     percentage: 100
   ```
3. Call:
   ```yaml
   service: fan.set_percentage
   target:
     entity_id: fan.example_fan
   data:
     percentage: 0
   ```
4. Observe the resulting state.

## Expected behavior

Setting `percentage: 0` should turn the fan off (`state: off`), per the documented `FanEntity` contract ("If percentage is set to 0, the fan should turn off").

## Actual behavior

The fan stays `on`, and `percentage` is clamped up to the lowest non-zero step (33% in my case) instead of the fan turning off. Verified this is stable, not a transient race — state stayed at `on` / 33% for 10+ seconds after the call.

By contrast, calling `fan.turn_off` directly on the same entity works correctly and reliably turns the fan off.

## Root cause (as far as I can tell)

In `homeassistant/components/tuya/fan.py`, `TuyaFanEntity.async_set_percentage`:

```python
@override
async def async_set_percentage(self, percentage: int) -> None:
    """Set the speed of the fan, as a percentage."""
    await self._async_send_wrapper_updates(self._speed_wrapper, percentage)
```

This forwards `percentage` straight to the speed wrapper with no special case for `0`. For an enum-backed speed wrapper with no "off" member, `0` gets rounded/clamped up to the lowest valid enum value instead of triggering `async_turn_off()`. Other Fan platforms in core generally guard this case explicitly, e.g.:

```python
async def async_set_percentage(self, percentage: int) -> None:
    if percentage == 0:
        await self.async_turn_off()
        return
    ...
```

Adding an equivalent guard here would fix it for any enum-speed Tuya fan, not just this specific product.

## Environment

- **Home Assistant Core**: 2026.9.1 (Supervisor install)
- **Integration**: Tuya (built-in, `homeassistant/components/tuya`) — cloud/device-sharing based, *not* the `tuya_local`/HACS custom integration
- **Device**: Brilliant Smart 99333 ceiling fan controller (Tuya `product_id: q0czoqfxdjynmkgj`, `product_name: "Brilliant Fan"`, category `fsd`); `fan_speed` DP is `Enum` with range `["1","2","3"]` (no continuous range)
- **Entity**: `fan.example_fan`

## Additional information

This likely affects **any** Tuya fan whose `fan_speed` DP is an `Enum` rather than an `Integer`/continuous range — the bug is in the generic wrapper handling, not specific to one product. Happy to provide diagnostics or test a patch if useful.

## Prior-issue search

Before filing, I searched `home-assistant/core` for existing reports of this behavior and reviewed the closest candidates in detail. None match — this appears to be a new issue against the current (wrapper-based) Tuya integration implementation:

- [#135541 — Tuya Fan doesn't support turn on and off](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/135541) (closed, not planned) — different symptom: `fan.turn_on`/`fan.turn_off` were entirely unsupported on the entity. Not a `percentage: 0` mapping issue.
- [#116213 — Tuya fan shown unavailable with percentage exception logged](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/116213) (closed, not planned) — different root cause: a type mismatch (device returned integer `1`, integration expected string `'1'`) causing the entity to show `unavailable`. Not related to the 0%→33% behavior.
- [#60521 — Tuya Fan Speed Control (Skyfan)](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/60521) — general/missing speed control against the older (pre-rewrite) integration, predates the current `tuya-device-handlers`-based architecture.
- [#66677 — Tuya Integration cannot control speed of Treatlife Ceiling Fan DS02F](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/66677) — same, older architecture, different symptom (speed control not working at all rather than 0%→lowest-step).
- [#133400 — Missing Fan Speed Control in Tuya Integration](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/133400) — again, missing speed control generally, not the specific "0% snaps to lowest step, state stays on" behavior.

None describe `fan.set_percentage(percentage: 0)` leaving the fan `on` and clamped to the lowest enum speed step instead of turning it off, so this looks like a distinct, previously unreported issue.

query:
time_simple_moving_average on high-frequency sensor blocks startup and causes unrelated integrations to time out

### The problem

A Filter helper using time_simple_moving_average with a 24-hour window on a high-frequency source sensor caused Home Assistant startup to take more than 7 minutes and triggered Bootstrap stage 2 timeout.

The source sensor (sensor.starlink_puissance) produces approximately one state every 5.1 seconds, or 16,945 states per 24 hours.

With the filter enabled:

filter setup: ~378–409 s
ZHA setup:    ~380–396 s
HA startup:   ~442–458 s

ZHA was cancelled by the global bootstrap timeout, and on some starts the automation list appeared empty.

Disabling only this Filter helper reduced startup to ~87 seconds and ZHA initialized normally in ~33 seconds.

I then replaced the configuration with two separate Filter helpers:

high-frequency source
→ time_throttle: 1 minute
→ time_simple_moving_average: 24 hours

After this change:

filter setup: 0.32 s
ZHA setup:    32.5 s
HA startup:   84.3 s

Subsequent startups remain normal (~2 minutes), with ZHA and automations loading correctly.

This suggests that restoring/replaying a large number of states for a long-window time_simple_moving_average during startup can block stage 2 long enough for unrelated integrations to be cancelled by the global bootstrap timeout.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.9.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Unknown / issue has existed across multiple Core versions

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Filter

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/filter/

### Diagnostics information

Source sensor:
sensor.starlink_puissance

Original Filter helper:
filter: time_simple_moving_average
window_size: 24 hours
type: last
precision: 0

Database measurement:
states last 24h: 16945
average states/hour: 706
average interval: 5.1 s

### Additional information

The Filter documentation currently warns about startup impact for large non-time window_size values, but this issue occurred with a time-based time_simple_moving_average window. It may be useful to review whether time-based filters over very high-frequency entities need similar protection, downsampling, lazy restoration, or documentation.

query: The built-in prompt in llm.py instructs the LLM Agent to use an incorrect name for the GetLiveContext tool (breaking GetLiveContext) ### The problem # Assist LLM tool names can differ from names referenced in built-in prompt ## The problem Since the LLM tool-namespacing changes introduced in Home Assistant 2026.9, the built-in instructions supplied to an Assist LLM can reference a tool name that does not match the actual name of the tool exposed to the LLM. A concrete example is `GetLiveContext`. The Home Assistant LLM platform defines the tool as: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` and its built-in dynamic prompt instructs the LLM to call: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` However, when the tool is exposed through the Assist API, it is additionally namespaced and the actual tool available to the LLM is: ```text assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` This creates a situation where the LLM can receive an explicit instruction to call a tool whose exact name does not exist in its tool registry. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Run Home Assistant Core 2026.9.1 with a local LLM conversation agent. 2. Use an Ollama-based conversation agent with the Home Assistant/Assist tools available. 3. Ask the agent a question requiring live Home Assistant state, such as: > What is on? 4. When the model follows the built-in `GetLiveContext` instruction, it may attempt to call: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` 5. Home Assistant returns: ```text HomeAssistantError: Tool "homeassistant__GetLiveContext" not found ``` The correctly namespaced tool is: ```text assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` and calling that exact name succeeds and returns the expected live context. I verified this directly with the same conversation agent: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext → Tool "homeassistant__GetLiveContext" not found assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext → successful Live Context response ``` I also asked the LLM to enumerate its available tools using their exact names. The registry contained: ```text assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` and did not contain: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` ## Why this appears to happen There appear to be two separate naming layers involved. The Home Assistant LLM platform defines the tool with the integration/domain prefix: ```text homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` The Assist API subsequently applies its own API namespace to tools, resulting in: ```text assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` The built-in dynamic prompt, however, still contains the original tool name. This means the final LLM context can effectively contain: ```text Instruction: You MUST call homeassistant__GetLiveContext. Available tool: assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` The `assist__` namespace may be completely intentional and useful. I am not suggesting that the namespace itself is incorrect. The problem is that the natural-language instructions and the actual tool registry can disagree about the canonical tool name. ## Impact This creates an unnecessary source of ambiguity and can cause failed tool calls even though the correct tool is available and functioning. It can also cause the LLM to spend additional reasoning/context processing trying to reconcile conflicting information, retrying failed tool calls, or explaining why a tool cannot be found. More generally, an internally generated instruction that contradicts the actual tool registry reduces the reliability and predictability of the Assist tool-calling system. ## Expected behavior Any tool name referenced in instructions supplied to an LLM should correspond to the canonical name actually exposed to that LLM. More generally, internally generated LLM instructions should not contain implementation-specific tool names that can become stale when the framework subsequently namespaces or transforms those tools. If the framework needs to instruct the model to use a tool, the tool name used in that instruction should ideally be derived from the same canonical tool definition/registry that is ultimately exposed to the model. ## Broader concern: internally generated hidden instructions This problem also highlights a broader architectural concern with the current Assist LLM implementation. Home Assistant injects internally generated instructions into the LLM context that are not visible in the administrator's configured system prompt. These instructions can materially affect the behavior of the LLM, yet the administrator has no supported way to inspect, modify, or disable them. This becomes particularly problematic when those instructions contain implementation-specific information, or when they contain behavioral instructions that may overlap with or conflict with the administrator's own system prompt. For example, internally generated instructions that tell the model how it should behave, how it should use Home Assistant tools, or that explicitly assert that particular tools exist are behavioral instructions rather than merely implementation metadata. I believe these internal instructions should either: 1. be exposed to the administrator so they can be inspected and modified; or 2. be reduced to the minimum instructions required for the Assist framework to function. In particular, tool metadata and tool names should ideally have a single canonical source of truth rather than being duplicated in independently maintained natural-language instructions. This would prevent exactly the type of inconsistency described in this report. There is already a separate feature discussion concerning administrator control over the hidden Assist system prompt: https://github.com/orgs/home-assistant/discussions/2322 I consider that discussion related but distinct from this bug. The feature request concerns administrator control over internally generated prompts; this report concerns a concrete functional inconsistency between an internally generated instruction and the actual tool registry. ## Relevant source The built-in Home Assistant LLM implementation is located at: `homeassistant/components/homeassistant/llm.py` It defines both the `GetLiveContext` tool and the dynamic instructions that tell the LLM how to use it. The Assist LLM framework subsequently applies API-level namespacing to the tools. The resulting tool name therefore differs from the name embedded in the original prompt. ## Environment * Home Assistant Core: 2026.9.1 * Home Assistant OS: 18.2 * Conversation agent: local Ollama * Installation: Home Assistant OS VM ## Summary The recent tool-prefix changes themselves may be correct. The bug is that the final tool name exposed to the LLM and the tool name referenced by Home Assistant's own generated instructions are not necessarily the same. In this case: ```text Built-in instruction: homeassistant__GetLiveContext Actual registered tool: assist__homeassistant__GetLiveContext ``` One fails with `Tool not found`; the other works. The generated instructions and the final tool registry should remain consistent. --- [chat-example-1.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32137662/chat-example-1.txt) [chat-example-2.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32137663/chat-example-2.txt) ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? core-2026.9.1 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? query:
iCloud device_tracker location frozen after startup (battery still updates) — pyicloud ≥2.3.0 no longer locates implicitly

### The problem

The iCloud integration's `device_tracker` entities stop receiving fresh GPS locations after Home Assistant starts: the coordinates (and `gps_accuracy`, bit-for-bit identical float) stay frozen for hours or days, while the battery sensors of the same devices update correctly on every poll. In my recorder history a phone's iCloud tracker kept the exact same lat/lon/accuracy for ~10 hours across two real-world trips (a companion-app tracker on the same phone followed the trips correctly), then jumped to the correct position immediately after an HA restart.

Root cause: a behavior change in pyicloud 2.3.0 (PR timlaing/pyicloud#175). Before it, `AppleDevice.status()`/`.location` implicitly called `refresh_client()` which always sent `"shouldLocate": true`, so every `IcloudAccount.update_devices()` poll actively located the devices — that is what the integration has relied on since the pyicloud 1.x days. Since 2.3.0, reads are pure cache reads and the library's background monitor thread refreshes with `locate=False`; the only active locate happens once when the service is constructed (i.e. at HA startup / integration reload). Apple then keeps serving its cached location blob — battery stays fresh (devices push status to Apple on their own), GPS never refreshes. Reported upstream too: timlaing/pyicloud#360.

The bug therefore ships in every HA release since the pyicloud 2.3.0 bump (#161164, HA 2026.2). It is completely silent — no errors, nothing in logs.

Fix: call the (since pyicloud 2.x) public `refresh(locate=True)` in `IcloudAccount.update_devices()` before reading device status. One-line change; I have been running it in production and the very next poll after deploying it un-froze the stale trackers (fresh accuracy values on every subsequent poll, device correctly moved into the right zone). PR incoming.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.1 (present since core-2026.2, the pyicloud 2.3.0 bump)

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2026.1.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Apple iCloud

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/icloud

_No response_

_No response_

```txt
Nothing - the failure is silent. Recorder history shows the symptom (battery changes each
30-min poll, GPS bit-for-bit identical):

09:28:07  lat=50.72648 lon=23.25166 gps_accuracy=9.280551647491146 battery=87
08:58:07  lat=50.72648 lon=23.25166 gps_accuracy=9.280551647491146 battery=97

```

### Additional information

Timeline of the regression:
- pyicloud 1.0.0 → 2.2.0: `AppleDevice.status()` / `.location` refreshed with `shouldLocate: true` on every access → each `update_devices()` poll actively located devices.
- pyicloud PR timlaing/pyicloud#175 (released in 2.3.0): removed the implicit refresh from `status()`/`location` and moved refreshing to a background thread that never passes `locate=True`.
- HA #161164 bumped to pyicloud 2.3.0 (core-2026.2) → locations freeze after startup for all users of this integration.

Blink integration repeatedly downloads duplicate MP4 clips on every coordinator refresh causing excessive bandwidth usage

### The problem

tl;dr: The current Blink integration downloads the same videos over and over again every 5 minutes, wasting massive amounts of bandwidth (nearly 1 TB/month for me and I'm sure Blink/Amazon isn't happy about it either). The culprit is that Home Assistant calls BlinkPy's refresh(force=True) on every scheduled refresh, which BlinkPy propagates as force_cache=True, causing already-cached videos to be downloaded again. There is a separate design question that may need to be addressed in another issue (which is whether the Blink integration should pre-fetch every new video at all when those videos are not stored or exposed for playback by default.)

## Summary

I discovered this after observing approximately **230 GB of downstream traffic from Blink (`rest-u###.immedia-semi.com`) to my Home Assistant host in approximately one week**.

My Blink account contains **14 cameras**, many of them newer 2K models. I am not using Home Assistant to archive Blink video, and I am not invoking `blink.save_video`, `blink.record`, `blink.save_recent_clips`, or other video-related actions. 

Investigation showed that normal five-minute Blink integration polling was downloading full motion-video MP4s. More importantly, I verified that **the same MP4 objects are downloaded repeatedly on successive polling cycles when no newer recording exists**.

This was confirmed both by the extremely high volume of traffic from the Home Assistant host to Blink's servers and by enabling `blinkpy.api` DEBUG logging and observing identical `cv_motion/<media_id>.mp4` URLs being requested repeatedly at five-minute intervals.

For example, multiple relatively inactive cameras were observed downloading a new MP4 after a motion event and then downloading that **exact same MP4 again on subsequent five-minute integration refreshes** when no new motion recording had occurred. Other cameras downloaded the same unchanged MP4 across several consecutive refresh cycles.

## Relevant code path

The behavior appears to result from the interaction between Home Assistant's routine use of `force=True` and BlinkPy's handling of that flag.

### Home Assistant forces every scheduled Blink refresh

`homeassistant/components/blink/coordinator.py` currently uses a 300-second polling interval:

```python
SCAN_INTERVAL = 300
```

and performs each scheduled refresh with:

```python
async def _async_update_data(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return await self.api.refresh(force=True)
```

Thus an ordinary scheduled integration update is not a normal BlinkPy refresh; it is always forced.

### BlinkPy turns `force=True` into `force_cache=True`

BlinkPy's `Blink.refresh()` has separate `force` and `force_cache` arguments:

```python
async def refresh(self, force=False, force_cache=False):
```

but when refreshing each Sync Module it does:

```python
await sync_module.refresh(force_cache=(force or force_cache))
```

Therefore, Home Assistant's routine:

```python
refresh(force=True)
```

ultimately results in:

```python
force_cache=True
```

being propagated into camera updates.

### BlinkPy deliberately preserves the previous video record

When checking for new videos, BlinkPy retains a camera's previous last record if no new motion recording has been found:

```python
# We want to keep the last record when no new motion was detected.
for camera in self.cameras:
    if len(self.last_records[camera]) == 0:
        if camera in last_record:
            self.last_records[camera].append(last_record[camera])
```

This means that after a camera has produced a qualifying clip, that old clip remains available as its `last_record` even when nothing new has happened.

### `force_cache=True` causes the retained MP4 to be downloaded again

In `blinkpy/camera.py`, the MP4 URL is obtained from that retained record.

BlinkPy appears to contain normal logic intended to avoid unnecessary video-cache updates:

```python
update_cached_video = False
if self._cached_video is None or self.motion_detected:
    update_cached_video = True
```

However, the actual download condition is:

```python
if clip_addr is not None and (update_cached_video or force_cache):
    response = await self.get_media(media_type="video")
    if response and response.status == 200:
        self._cached_video = await response.read()
```

Because Home Assistant's normal scheduled refresh ultimately supplies `force_cache=True`, the normal cache/update test is bypassed.

The result appears to be:

```text
camera records video
        |
        v
last_records[camera] contains MP4
        |
        v
MP4 downloaded
        |
        v
no subsequent motion
        |
        v
previous last_record retained
        |
        v
next five-minute HA refresh uses force=True
        |
        v
BlinkPy receives force_cache=True
        |
        v
same MP4 downloaded again
        |
        v
repeat
```

This behavior matches the observed network traffic and BlinkPy HTTP GET logging.

## Impact

There are **288 scheduled Blink refreshes per day** at a five-minute interval.

On my installation, the resulting traffic was approximately:

* **230 GB/week**
* approximately **1 TB/month** at the observed rate

The exact impact will obviously depend on camera count, resolution, clip length, and motion frequency. However, the problematic part is that after a video has been cached, an inactive camera can continue transferring that same multi-megabyte video every five minutes even though nothing has changed.

This also generates unnecessary media requests and unnecessary Blink server egress.

## Expected behavior

Routine Home Assistant polling should not re-download a video that is already cached and has not changed.

At minimum, the purpose of Home Assistant's `force=True` appears to need to be separated from BlinkPy's `force_cache=True` behavior.

If Home Assistant needs to bypass BlinkPy's ordinary API-refresh throttle so that the HA coordinator controls polling, that should not also require bypassing the media cache and downloading unchanged MP4 files.

The exact implementation is best determined by the maintainers, but an unchanged `clip_addr` / media ID should not result in repeated full-video transfers every five minutes.

## Related but separate design question: should videos be pre-fetched at all?

There is also a broader issue that I do **not** think needs to block resolution of the duplicate-download bug above.

Even if repeated downloads of unchanged clips are fixed, the integration currently appears to automatically download each newly detected Blink MP4 during routine polling.

That means Home Assistant can effectively act as a second consumer of every video generated by a Blink system, even when the user has never asked Home Assistant to retrieve, save, or archive that video.

The Home Assistant Blink camera entity exposes the cached still image but does not expose these automatically cached MP4s as directly playable media. Video-related behavior is instead available through explicit actions such as saving clips.

It therefore seems worth separately considering whether downloading every newly generated video should be the default behavior at all, or whether video retrieval should instead be:

* lazy/on-demand;
* triggered only by explicit video-related actions; or
* separately configurable.

For installations with many cameras, eagerly pre-fetching every Blink video can silently add substantial WAN traffic and Blink server egress even after the duplicate-download bug is fixed.

I am treating these as two distinct questions:

**This issue:** The same unchanged MP4 is demonstrably downloaded repeatedly during five-minute polling. This appears to be an implementation bug.

**Possible separate issue:** Should Home Assistant automatically pre-fetch every new Blink MP4 in the first place?

If maintainers consider the second concern distinct, I can open a separate issue for it.

## Reproduction

1. Configure the standard Home Assistant Blink integration with polling enabled.
2. Use a camera that has recently generated a motion recording.
3. Ensure no newer recording is generated.
4. Observe network requests made by the Home Assistant host during successive five-minute Blink refreshes.
5. The same `cv_motion/<media_id>.mp4` resource is retrieved repeatedly despite no change to the video.

I reproduced this independently on multiple cameras, including relatively inactive cameras where the transition from a newly generated recording to repeated retrieval of the unchanged recording was easy to observe.

query:
Ring reauthentication discards saved push listener credentials

### The problem

The Ring integration stores its Firebase/FCM listener credentials in the config entry under `listen_token`. Completing either the reauthentication flow or the reconfigure flow replaces the complete config-entry data mapping with only `username`, the new Ring API token, and `device_id`.

That silently deletes `listen_token`. On the next setup, the integration must create a new Google push-registration identity instead of checking in with the saved one. This makes a Ring account reauthentication unexpectedly reset a separate, working push identity and can leave the Ding/motion event entities unavailable if fresh GCM registration is rejected.

The problem is deterministic in current code:

1. Let the Ring integration persist listener credentials through its credentials-updated callback.
2. Complete Ring reauthentication or reconfiguration.
3. Inspect the updated config entry: `listen_token` is gone.
4. Reload starts the full FCM registration path instead of reusing the stored listener credentials.

Reauthentication should update only the Ring authentication fields. Reconfiguration may rotate the Ring `device_id`, but the independent FCM credentials can still be checked in and subscribed under the newly authorized Ring device; if check-in fails, the dependency already falls back to full registration.

Using `data_updates=` rather than `data=` in both flows preserves `listen_token` and any future unrelated config-entry fields while still replacing the three intended values.

2026.9.2; current `dev` at `2f79d1f` has the same behavior.

Unknown

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Ring

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/ring/

### Diagnostics information

No diagnostics are attached because the affected config-entry fields contain credentials. The behavior is covered by config-flow regression tests that seed a sanitized `listen_token` value and verify it survives both successful flows.

This is separate from receiver-health failures such as #157764 and #173299. It does not itself make Google accept a new registration; it prevents a normal Ring authentication action from unnecessarily forcing one.

query:
Live Context reports a light's brightness as 0-255 while the light tool accepts 0-100, so a model doing arithmetic on what it read sends an out-of-range value

### The problem

The live context and the light tool use different units for the same quantity, so a model that reads a light's brightness and computes a new value from it sends a number the tool refuses.

**What the model is shown.** `homeassistant__GetLiveContext` renders each exposed entity's interesting attributes, and `brightness` is one of them. The value is the state attribute exactly as stored, on the 0-255 scale, with no conversion (`homeassistant/components/homeassistant/llm.py` at tag 2026.9.2: the `interesting_attributes` set at lines 81-95, the attribute copy at lines 159-170, which stringifies `Enum`, `Decimal` and `int` values and changes nothing else). Inside core that rendering is read only by `GetLiveContext`'s `async_call` (line 253) and the Assist API's static prompt (line 328).

```yaml
- names: <one exposed light>
  domain: light
  state: 'on'
  attributes:
    brightness: '255'
```

**What the model must then send.** `HassLightSet`'s `brightness` slot is a percentage (`homeassistant/components/light/intent.py`, lines 37-45):

```python
"brightness": intent.IntentSlotInfo(
    service_data_name=ATTR_BRIGHTNESS_PCT,
    description="The brightness percentage of the light between 0 and 100, where 0 is off and 100 is fully lit",
    value_schema=vol.All(vol.Coerce(int), vol.Range(0, 100)),
),
```

A model asked for a relative change reads 255, halves it, and sends 127: correct arithmetic on the number it was shown, and a value `vol.Range(0, 100)` rejects.

**To reproduce:** expose one light at full brightness to a conversation agent that uses the LLM tool API and can call a tool, read the result and answer again. Ask it to make that light half as bright. The model calls `GetLiveContext`, is told `brightness: '255'`, and calls `HassLightSet` with `brightness: 127`. An absolute request ("set it to fifty percent") does not show it, because the model never reads the current value.

**What models actually sent**, over 529 requests per model with Home Assistant's own prompt and tools unchanged, temperature 0: Gemma 4 12B, asked five differently worded times to halve a light at 255, sent `brightness: 127` five out of five. Asked five times to take it down by twenty percent, it sent 191, 235, 180, 178 and 195, all arithmetic on the 0-255 scale, all outside the tool's range. The same model got every thermostat change right (69 and 66 from a target of 68) and five of five fan-speed changes right, because temperature and a fan's `percentage` read the same in the live context and in the tool. It is right whenever the two halves agree on the unit and wrong whenever they do not.

**The value really is refused.** On my instance (2026.9.2), `POST /api/intent/handle` with `{"name": "HassLightSet", "data": {"name": "<one exposed light>", "brightness": 127}}` was refused before any service call; the light did not change (log below). The same call with `brightness: 50` succeeded and the light read back 128. On the model's path, `IntentTool.async_call` (`homeassistant/helpers/llm.py` 255-296) calls `intent.async_handle` with no `try`, and `conversation/chat_log.py` 460-465 returns `{"error": "InvalidSlotInfo", ...}` to the model, so the conversation wastes a turn rather than doing nothing silently. The model measurements above were made against a harness that does not run the intent handlers; the refusal was confirmed separately against the real instance.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Home Assistant Core Integration (homeassistant), LLM API

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homeassistant

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.intent] Received invalid slot info for HassLightSet: value must be at most 100 at 'brightness.value'
```

### Additional information

**Two ways to fix it, with what each costs.**

1. Render brightness as a percentage in the live context, so what the model reads is in the same units as what it must send. Cost: it changes what existing prompts show, so anything tuned to the raw 0-255 value could break.
2. Add a percentage field beside the raw one, for example `brightness_pct` alongside `brightness`. Cost: two values for one quantity, and the raw one is of no use to the model, since the only light tool takes a percentage and a person asking how bright a light is cannot use 255 either.

What I would do: ship the second now so nothing breaks, and deprecate the raw rendering with a removal release announced so anyone depending on it has time to move. I have the change with a test ready and will open a PR if that shape is acceptable.

**The general shape** is that the live context renders whatever unit the entity stores while the tools take percentages. Brightness is the case I measured. **A media player looks worse and quieter:** `volume_level` is rendered as the raw 0.0-1.0 float (the copy at llm.py 159-170 leaves a float alone), while `HassSetVolume`'s slot is `vol.All(vol.Coerce(int), vol.Range(min=0, max=100), lambda val: val / 100)` (`media_player/intent.py` 121-128; the relative handler at 411-419). A model that reads `volume_level: 0.5` and halves it sends 0.25, which `vol.Coerce(int)` turns into 0 and the range accepts: muted, not refused. Read in the source, not measured.

**A smaller separate bug** met while confirming the refusal: the REST endpoint answered HTTP 500, because `IntentHandleView.post` (`components/intent/__init__.py` 676-682) catches `IntentHandleError` and `MatchFailedError` but not their sibling `InvalidSlotInfo` (`helpers/intent.py` 152-177). Noted here; happy to file it separately.

Flo: water temperature publishes a constant placeholder (225 °F) on devices that do not measure it

### The problem

On a Flo Smart Water Shutoff with no water-temperature sensor, the Flo API does not omit `tempF` — it returns a constant placeholder. The integration passes it through, so `sensor.*_water_temperature` publishes a fixed **225 °F** indefinitely, carrying `SensorDeviceClass.TEMPERATURE` and `SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT`. It is recorded, charted, and usable by automations and long-term statistics.

225 °F is above boiling and cannot occur in a supply line at atmospheric pressure.

### Evidence

Recorder data from one valve over nine days:

| entity | rows | distinct values |
|---|---|---|
| `*_water_temperature` | 70 | **2** — `225` (×60), `unavailable` (×10) |
| `*_water_flow` | 87 | 19 |
| `*_water_pressure` | 87 | 18 |

Flow and pressure vary normally across the same window, so the device is online and reporting. It does not measure temperature. The value was `225` while flow was `2.16 gal/min`, so it is not a zero-flow artifact.

### Code path

`homeassistant/components/flo/coordinator.py`:

```python
@property
def temperature(self) -> float:
    """Return the current temperature in degrees F."""
    return self._device_information["telemetry"]["current"]["tempF"]
```

`homeassistant/components/flo/sensor.py`:

```python
@property
def native_value(self) -> float | None:
    """Return the current temperature."""
    if self._device.temperature is None:
        return None
    return round(self._device.temperature, 1)
```

The only guard is for `None`. `FloTemperatureSensor(device, True)` is created for every non-`puck_oem` device whether or not the hardware measures temperature.

### Scope of what I tested

I do not run the core `flo` integration on this device. I reach the same API with my own client, which reads the identical field (`telemetry.current.tempF`). The core code path above is verified by reading it, not by observing core emit 225 on this hardware.

Distinct from #64150, which is a °C→°F conversion bug. There is no conversion here — the API returns Fahrenheit and the sensor declares Fahrenheit.

### Suggested fix

Reject physically impossible values rather than hard-coding one vendor sentinel, so a different placeholder is also caught:

```python
@property
def native_value(self) -> float | None:
    """Return the current temperature."""
    temperature = self._device.temperature
    if temperature is None or temperature >= 212:
        # Some valves have no temperature sensor and report a constant placeholder
        # (225 °F observed) instead of omitting the field. Water cannot reach boiling
        # in a supply line at atmospheric pressure.
        return None
    return round(temperature, 1)
```

`None` makes the entity unavailable instead of publishing a fixed number into history and automations.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2026.7.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

flo

### Link to integration documentation

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/flo/

+"""Repairs for Xbox integration."""
+
+from typing import cast
+
+import probatio
+
+from homeassistant.components.repairs import (
+    ConfirmRepairFlow,
+    RepairsFlow,
+    RepairsFlowResult,
+)
+from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
+from homeassistant.helpers import entity_registry as er
+from homeassistant.helpers.issue_registry import async_delete_issue
+
+from .const import DOMAIN
+
+
+class DeprecatedEntityRepairFlow(RepairsFlow):
+    """Handler for a deprecated entity issue fixing flow."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, issue_id: str, data: dict[str, str | int | float | None]
+    ) -> None:
+        """Initialize."""
+        self._data = data
+        self._issue_id = issue_id
+
+    async def async_step_init(
+        self, user_input: dict[str, str] | None = None
+    ) -> RepairsFlowResult:
+        """Handle the first step of a fix flow."""
+
+        return await self.async_step_confirm()
+
+    async def async_step_confirm(
+        self, user_input: dict[str, str] | None = None
+    ) -> RepairsFlowResult:
+        """Handle the confirm step of a fix flow."""
+        if user_input is not None:
+            er.async_get(self.hass).async_remove(cast(str, self._data["entity_id"]))
+            async_delete_issue(self.hass, DOMAIN, self._issue_id)
+            return self.async_create_entry(data={})
+
+        return self.async_show_form(step_id="confirm", data_schema=probatio.Schema({}))
+
+
+async def async_create_fix_flow(
+    hass: HomeAssistant, issue_id: str, data: dict[str, str | int | float | None] | None
+) -> RepairsFlow:
+    """Create flow."""
+    if not data or "entity_id" not in data:
+        raise ValueError("Missing data for repair flow")
+    return (
+        DeprecatedEntityRepairFlow(issue_id, data)
+        if issue_id.startswith("deprecated_entity_")
+        else ConfirmRepairFlow()
+    )

query:
Hive: setup forwards a filtered platform list but unload unloads all of them

### The problem

`async_setup_entry` forwards only the platforms that have devices:

```python
await hass.config_entries.async_forward_entry_setups(
    entry,
    [ha_type for ha_type, hive_type in PLATFORM_LOOKUP.items() if devices.get(hive_type)],
)
```

but `async_unload_entry` unloads the full constant:

```python
return await hass.config_entries.async_unload_platforms(entry, PLATFORMS)
```

This asymmetry has two independent consequences.

**1. Entity services disappear along with their devices.** `climate.py` and `water_heater.py` register their services *inside* the platform's `async_setup_entry`, after the device guard:

```python
devices = hive.session.deviceList.get("water_heater")
if devices:
    async_add_entities(...)

platform = entity_platform.async_get_current_platform()
platform.async_register_entity_service(SERVICE_BOOST_HOT_WATER, ...)
```

Because the platform is only forwarded when devices exist, an account that returns no water-heater device never registers `hive.boost_hot_water` at all. Automations calling it fail with `Action hive.boost_hot_water not found` and there is no other indication. Service availability should not be coupled to device discovery.

**2. Reload fails outright for any account missing a platform.** On an account with no Hive bulbs, unloading `light` raises `ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!`. The unload fails and the entry lands in `FAILED_UNLOAD`, which HA then refuses to reload (`Entry cannot be reloaded`), leaving the integration dead until a full restart. Reproduced on 2026.9.3 with an account whose setup logged `0 light`.

#176594 makes that second symptom non-fatal on `dev` (warn and return `True`), but it does not address the asymmetry — it converts it into a spurious warning on *every* reload for the common case of a user with no Hive bulbs or smart plugs.

Suggested fix: record the platforms actually forwarded (for example on `entry.runtime_data`) and unload exactly those.

Note that the obvious simplification — forwarding all of `PLATFORMS` unconditionally — is not safe as-is. `light`, `switch`, `sensor`, `climate` and `water_heater` all guard the empty case, but `binary_sensor.py` iterates unguarded and would raise `TypeError` if the key is absent rather than empty:

```python
devices = hive.session.deviceList.get("binary_sensor")
sensors.extend(... for dev in devices ...)   # for dev in None
```

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2026.9.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Not a regression — long-standing behaviour.

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Hive

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/hive

### Diagnostics information

Hive does not implement diagnostics, so none are available.

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml

```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
10:19:00 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.hive] Error unloading entry *****@**** for light
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "homeassistant/config_entries.py", line 1046, in async_unload
    result = await component.async_unload_entry(hass, self)
  File "homeassistant/components/light/__init__.py", line 567, in async_unload_entry
    return await hass.data[DATA_COMPONENT].async_unload_entry(entry)
  File "homeassistant/helpers/entity_component.py", line 201, in async_unload_entry
    raise ValueError("Config entry was never loaded!")
ValueError: Config entry was never loaded!

# the entry is now unreloadable:
{"message": "Entry cannot be reloaded"}
```

### Additional information

Possibly the same root cause, both closed without diagnosis:

- #121726 — the Hive water heater keeps only its registry capability attributes (`min_temp`, `max_temp`, `operation_list`) after a reload, losing `supported_features` and `operation_mode`. That is the entity-registry-placeholder signature, i.e. the `water_heater` platform was not set up after the reload.
- #75639 — water heater entity absent entirely on a thermostat-only account.

Core-side context for the unload symptom: #176593 / #176594 (tolerance for unloading a never-loaded entry, merged to `dev` 2026-09-08, not present in any 2026.9.x tag) and #176652 (setup-side root cause, open). This issue is the integration-side asymmetry those leave in place.

Fix swallowed exceptions in lifx_cloud action handlers

The `lifx_cloud` integration catches exceptions in action handlers but only logs them instead of re-raising. This means the user gets no feedback in the UI when an action fails, and automations continue executing as if the action succeeded.

**Affected methods in `scene.py`:**
- `async_activate` (scene.py)

**How to fix:**

Replace the `except` blocks that only log with ones that raise `HomeAssistantError`:

```python
# Before (bad)
except SomeError as err:
    _LOGGER.error("Failed: %s", err)

# After (good)
except SomeError as err:
    raise HomeAssistantError(
        translation_domain=DOMAIN,
        translation_key="failed_to_turn_on",
    ) from err
```

Add the corresponding translation keys to `strings.json`. After fixing, remove the `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-action-swallowed-exception` comments.

Thanks for sharing @permissionBRICK, I am now using a version of this to resolve the issue. 

I ported it to a Cloudflare Worker (TypeScript) so it runs on the edge with no server to maintain.

Key changes from your original:

- TZID/DST preservation for recurring events — converting to UTC caused duplicate events when an occurrence was edited (both the original and the modified version would show up, because the EXDATE couldn't match across DST boundaries)
- Token-based auth to prevent the worker being used as an open proxy

HomematicIP Cloud config flow: button confirmation triggers no network request, flow silently closes

### Checklist

- [x] I have updated to the latest available Home Assistant version.
- [x] I have cleared the cache of my browser.
- [x] I have tried a different browser to see if it is related to my browser.
- [x] I have tried reproducing the issue in [safe mode](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2023/11/01/release-202311/#restarting-into-safe-mode) to rule out problems with unsupported custom resources.

### Describe the issue you are experiencing

When setting up the HomematicIP Cloud integration, after entering the SGTIN and reaching the step that asks to press the physical button on the Access Point, clicking "OK" triggers no visible action. The config flow dialog just closes silently, without any error message.

Using Chrome DevTools (Network tab, both WebSocket messages and Fetch/XHR), I confirmed that clicking "OK" after pressing the physical Access Point button triggers zero network activity — no websocket message, no HTTP request at all. The popup simply closes.

Troubleshooting already performed:
- Confirmed Access Point and Home Assistant are on the same network segment (no VLAN/guest isolation)
- Replaced the Access Point with a new HmIP-HAP2 (previous unit was a first-generation 2016 model) — same result

- Confirmed the official Homematic IP mobile app works normally and can control all devices
- No relevant entries in home-assistant.log, even with debug logging enabled for homematicip_cloud and homeassistant.helpers.aiohttp_client

### Describe the behavior you expected

After pressing the physical button on the Access Point and clicking "OK", I expected the config flow to send a request to complete the cloud pairing (or at minimum show an error message if it failed), and eventually create a working HomematicIP Cloud config entry with all my devices.

2. Search for and select "HomematicIP Cloud"

4. Click Submit/Next
5. Wait for the prompt asking to press the blue button on the Access Point
6. Press the physical button on the Access Point
7. Click "OK" in the dialog
8. Expected: the flow completes (or shows an error). Actual: the dialog closes silently, no network request is sent (confirmed via DevTools), and nothing appears in the logs.

core-2026.9.2
